# Your first model call in 5 minutes

Azure AI Gateway gives your apps and agents one governed endpoint for models and tools. In five minutes you create a
gateway, put a Microsoft Foundry model behind it, and call that model the way an app does: with the gateway's URL, an
alias in the `model` field, and a runtime API key. Click through the AI Gateway portal, paste a few Azure CLI
commands into Azure Cloud Shell, or deploy a Bicep template with one `azd up`. There's nothing to clone or install.

![Create the gateway, a Foundry model, a provider, an alias, and a runtime key in the AI Gateway portal, with the Azure CLI in Cloud Shell, or with a Bicep template and azd up. Then your app calls the alias with the key, and the gateway routes the call to Foundry with its managed identity](../assets/diagrams/quickstart.svg "Set up once, in the portal, in Cloud Shell, or with azd up. Then every call goes through the gateway: it checks the key, routes the alias, and signs in to Foundry with its own identity.")

## Before you begin

You need an Azure subscription where you can create resources and role assignments, for example **Owner**, or
**Contributor** plus **Role Based Access Control Administrator**. The gateway gets a role on your Foundry account, so
that it can call the model with its own identity. Each track lists the tools that it needs at its start.

## How it works

Every call that goes through AI Gateway uses the same five building blocks. In this quick start you create one of
each.

| Building block | What it does | In this quick start |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Gateway** | The Azure resource (`Microsoft.ApiManagement/aigateways`) that gives your apps one runtime URL for models and tools | Your gateway, at `https://<gateway>.<location>-01.ai.gateway.azure.com` |
| **Model provider** | A connection to a backend. The gateway signs in to it with its own managed identity, so your apps never hold a backend key | Your Foundry account. The Azure CLI and Bicep tracks name the provider `foundry-models` |
| **Model** | A backend deployment that the gateway can route to | The Foundry deployment `gpt-6-luna` |
| **Alias** | The name that apps send in the `model` field. The gateway routes the alias to one or more models | `<foundry-account-name>/gpt-6-luna` in the portal, `gpt-6-luna` in the Azure CLI and Bicep tracks |
| **Runtime API key** | Identifies the app that calls the gateway, for limits, cost, and monitoring | `app-first-call` |

Your app calls the OpenAI-compatible base URL `<gateway URL>/default/models/openai/v1`, so any OpenAI SDK works with
a different base URL and the runtime key. For the full tour, watch the 3-minute video in
[How Azure AI Gateway works](../00-how-ai-gateway-works/README.md).

## Create a gateway and make your first call

Pick one track. Each one creates the same five building blocks, makes your first call through the gateway, and ends
with how to clean up.
During the preview, AI Gateway runs in East US 2 (`eastus2`) and Sweden Central (`swedencentral`).

<!-- track: portal | Portal -->

**What you need:** a browser, and a model deployment in a Microsoft Foundry account, for example `gpt-6-luna`.

<details>
<summary>No Foundry deployment yet? Create one in Cloud Shell.</summary>

Open [Azure Cloud Shell](https://shell.azure.com) in Bash and paste these commands. They create a Foundry account with
a `gpt-6-luna` deployment in a new resource group, in a minute or two. Then create the gateway in the same resource
group, so that you can clean up with one command. Model inference is billed per use.

```bash title="Bash"
RG="rg-aigw-quickstart"; FOUNDRY="aigw$(openssl rand -hex 3)"
az group create --name "$RG" --location eastus2 --output none
az cognitiveservices account create --resource-group "$RG" --name "$FOUNDRY" --location eastus2 \
  --kind AIServices --sku S0 --custom-domain "$FOUNDRY" --yes --output none
az cognitiveservices account deployment create --resource-group "$RG" --name "$FOUNDRY" \
  --deployment-name gpt-6-luna --model-name gpt-6-luna --model-version 2026-09-22 --model-format OpenAI \
  --sku-name GlobalStandard --sku-capacity 10 --output none
echo "Foundry account $FOUNDRY in $RG"
```

</details>

### Create the gateway

1. Open the [AI Gateway portal](https://ai.gateway.azure.com) and sign in. For your first gateway, the portal opens
   **Create AI gateway** right away. Otherwise, open the gateway switcher in the top bar and select
   **Create new gateway**.

   ![The gateway switcher open in the top bar, with Recent gateways, View all gateways, and Create new gateway](../assets/screens/quickstart-01-switcher.webp "The gateway switcher lists your recent gateways. Create new gateway opens the Create AI gateway dialog.")

2. Enter a **Name**, or select **Generate a new name**. Then choose your **Subscription**, a **Resource group**, and
   the **Region**: **East US 2** or **Sweden Central**. For the resource group, select **New**, or select
   **Existing** and pick the resource group of your Foundry account, so that you can clean up both with one command.

   ![The Create AI gateway dialog with a name, the Existing resource group rg-aigw-quickstart, and the East US 2 region](../assets/screens/quickstart-02-create.webp "Create AI gateway: a generated name, the existing resource group of the Foundry account, and East US 2.")

3. Keep the **Advanced** defaults and select **Create gateway**. **All gateways** opens and shows the provisioning
   status, which moves from **Activating** to **Succeeded** in a few minutes. Then the portal selects your new
   gateway.

   ![All gateways with the banner Gateway creation is in progress and the new gateway in the Activating state](../assets/screens/quickstart-03-provisioning.webp "All gateways while the gateway provisions. You can keep using other gateways in the meantime.")

### Import the model from Foundry

1. **Home** opens with the **Set up your gateway** guide. Under **Add a model**, select
   **Add from Microsoft Foundry**.

   ![Home with the new gateway in the switcher and the Set up your gateway guide, with Add from Microsoft Foundry highlighted](../assets/screens/quickstart-04-home.webp "Set up your gateway walks you through three steps: add a model, test a model, and apply policies.")

   You can also start from **Models** › **Add** › **Models from Microsoft Foundry**.

   ![The Models page with the Add menu open on Models from Microsoft Foundry](../assets/screens/quickstart-05-add-menu.webp "Models › Add imports models from Microsoft Foundry or a custom provider, or creates an alias for a model that you already added.")

2. **Add models from Microsoft Foundry** discovers the model deployments in your subscriptions and selects all of
   them. In **Resource groups**, select only the resource group of your Foundry account. Then check that **Models**
   selects only your Foundry account with `gpt-6-luna`.
3. Keep **Managed identity** as the **Authentication method**, with the system-assigned managed identity, and keep
   **Create an alias for each model** selected. Then select **Add models**.

   ![Add models from Microsoft Foundry, filtered to one resource group, with Managed identity, Create an alias for each model, one selected Foundry account with gpt-6-luna, and the Add models button highlighted](../assets/screens/quickstart-06-import.webp "Filter by resource group, so that you import only the deployment that you need. The gateway calls Foundry with its managed identity.")

4. **Models** opens. The **Backend models** tab lists `gpt-6-luna`, and the **Aliases** tab shows the alias that
   apps call: `<foundry-account-name>/gpt-6-luna`. Note the alias.

   ![The Aliases tab of Models with the alias aigwb92bd1/gpt-6-luna, its backend model gpt-6-luna, and its provider](../assets/screens/quickstart-07-alias.webp "Each alias is named after the Foundry account and the deployment, and routes to the backend model gpt-6-luna.")

### Create a runtime API key

1. Select **Access**, then the **Keys** tab, then **Create API key**.

   ![Access with the Keys tab, the Create API key button, and the new key app-first-call in the list](../assets/screens/quickstart-08-keys.webp "Access › Keys lists the built-in all-access subscription and your keys. After the next step, app-first-call appears here.")

2. Enter `app-first-call` as the **Key name**, then select **Create**.

   ![The Create API key dialog with the key name app-first-call and the Create button](../assets/screens/quickstart-09-key-create.webp "Give the key a name that identifies the app. Limits, cost, and monitoring use it.")

3. In **API key created successfully**, select **Copy & done** to copy the key. Keep it somewhere safe: you paste it
   in the next steps. You can view, rotate, or delete it later in **Access** › **Keys**.

   ![The API key created successfully dialog with a masked key, the key name, and the Copy & done button](../assets/screens/quickstart-10-key-done.webp "The key stays masked until you select Show. Copy & done copies it and closes the dialog.")

### Make your first call

Call the model through the gateway in the playground, with your new key, the way an app does.

1. Select **Catalog**, then select your model.

   ![The Catalog with the model card aigwb92bd1/gpt-6-luna](../assets/screens/quickstart-11-catalog.webp "The Catalog lists the models and MCP servers that apps can call through this gateway.")

2. Under **Authentication**, choose `app-first-call` as the **API key**, so that the playground calls the gateway
   with your new key. Then send a prompt, for example `In one sentence, what does an AI gateway do?`.

   ![The model page with the API key app-first-call, the prompt, and the model's reply](../assets/screens/quickstart-12-playground.webp "The playground calls the gateway's endpoint with the key that you choose, and shows the reply, the latency, and the tokens.")

3. Optional: to make the same call from code, select **Continue in code**. It shows the endpoint URL and snippets
   for cURL, the OpenAI SDK, LangChain, Vercel AI, the GitHub Copilot SDK, and Microsoft Agent Framework, plus a
   prompt that installs the AI Gateway plugin in your coding agent.

   ![Continue in code with the cURL snippet selected, which calls the alias with the api-key header](../assets/screens/quickstart-13-code.webp "The cURL snippet has your gateway's URL and alias, and reads the key from the AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY environment variable.")

To run the cURL snippet, open [Azure Cloud Shell](https://shell.azure.com) in Bash, paste your key at this prompt so
that it never shows on screen, and then paste the snippet:

```bash title="Bash"
read -rsp "AI Gateway API key: " AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY && export AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY && echo
```

> **Checkpoint:** the playground answered with the key `app-first-call`. Your gateway is live, and your app never
> needs a Foundry key: only the gateway's managed identity calls Foundry.

### Clean up

To keep exploring, skip this step: [lab 03](../03-multi-provider-aliases/README.md) and the labs after it work on this
gateway. On the labs site, save the resource group and the gateway name in **Your values**. Otherwise, delete the
gateway.

1. Open the gateway switcher in the top bar and select **View all gateways**.

2. On your gateway's row, select **More actions** (**⋮**), and then select **Delete**.

   ![All gateways filtered to lucky-brook, with the More actions menu open on its row and Delete marked](../assets/screens/quickstart-14-delete.webp "The More actions menu on a gateway's row: open the gateway in the Azure portal, copy its resource ID, or delete it.")

3. To confirm, select **Delete** in the dialog. The row shows **Deleting** until Azure removes the gateway, in about
   five minutes.

   ![The dialog Delete "lucky-brook-5340"? with the Cancel and Delete buttons, and Delete marked](../assets/screens/quickstart-15-delete-confirm.webp "Deleting a gateway removes its models, aliases, keys, and policies. It can't be undone.")

Deleting the gateway keeps its resource group and your Foundry account. If you created them in Cloud Shell for this
quick start, delete the resource group and purge the Foundry account there too: deleted Foundry accounts stay
soft-deleted for 48 hours and keep counting against your quota until you purge them.

```bash title="Bash"
FOUNDRY="$(az cognitiveservices account list --resource-group rg-aigw-quickstart --query "[0].name" --output tsv)"
az group delete --name rg-aigw-quickstart --yes
az cognitiveservices account purge --name "$FOUNDRY" --resource-group rg-aigw-quickstart --location eastus2
```

> **Checkpoint:** after you refresh the page, **All gateways** no longer lists your gateway.

<!-- track: cli | Azure CLI -->

**What you need:** [Azure Cloud Shell](https://shell.azure.com), in Bash or PowerShell. It's already signed in and has
the Azure CLI, `curl`, and `jq`. A local Azure CLI 2.75 or later, signed in with `az login`, works too. The track
creates the Foundry deployment for you.

### Set your variables

Paste the block for your shell. A random suffix keeps the gateway and Foundry account names globally unique.

```bash title="Bash"
export RG="rg-aigw-quickstart"
export LOCATION="eastus2"                     # or swedencentral
SUFFIX="$(openssl rand -hex 3)"
export GATEWAY="aigw-$SUFFIX"                 # part of the runtime URL
export FOUNDRY="aigw$SUFFIX"                  # the Foundry account and its subdomain
export DEPLOYMENT="gpt-6-luna"
export PROVIDER="foundry-models"

export API="api-version=2025-09-01-preview"
export SUBSCRIPTION_ID="$(az account show --query id --output tsv)"
export GATEWAY_ID="/subscriptions/$SUBSCRIPTION_ID/resourceGroups/$RG/providers/Microsoft.ApiManagement/aigateways/$GATEWAY"
export GW="https://management.azure.com$GATEWAY_ID"
export WS="$GW/workspaces/default"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$RG         = "rg-aigw-quickstart"
$LOCATION   = "eastus2"                       # or swedencentral
$SUFFIX     = [guid]::NewGuid().ToString("N").Substring(0, 6)
$GATEWAY    = "aigw-$SUFFIX"                  # part of the runtime URL
$FOUNDRY    = "aigw$SUFFIX"                   # the Foundry account and its subdomain
$DEPLOYMENT = "gpt-6-luna"
$PROVIDER   = "foundry-models"

$API             = "api-version=2025-09-01-preview"
$SUBSCRIPTION_ID = az account show --query id --output tsv
$GATEWAY_ID      = "/subscriptions/$SUBSCRIPTION_ID/resourceGroups/$RG/providers/Microsoft.ApiManagement/aigateways/$GATEWAY"
$GW              = "https://management.azure.com$GATEWAY_ID"
$WS              = "$GW/workspaces/default"
```

### Start creating the gateway

Register the resource providers, which is a one-time step for each subscription, and create a resource group. Then
create the gateway and its companion connector gateway. Azure accepts the gateway and keeps provisioning it in the
background, so you can move on right away.

```bash title="Bash"
for ns in Microsoft.ApiManagement Microsoft.Web Microsoft.CognitiveServices; do az provider register --namespace "$ns" --wait; done
az group create --name "$RG" --location "$LOCATION" --output none

az rest --method put --output none \
  --url "https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/$SUBSCRIPTION_ID/resourceGroups/$RG/providers/Microsoft.Web/connectorGateways/$GATEWAY?api-version=2026-05-01-preview" \
  --body "$(jq -cn --arg l "$LOCATION" '{location: $l, properties: {}}')"
az rest --method put --output none --url "$GW?$API" \
  --body "$(jq -cn --arg l "$LOCATION" '{location: $l, identity: {type: "SystemAssigned"}, properties: {publicNetworkAccess: "Enabled"}}')"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
foreach ($ns in "Microsoft.ApiManagement", "Microsoft.Web", "Microsoft.CognitiveServices") { az provider register --namespace $ns --wait }
az group create --name $RG --location $LOCATION --output none

@{ location = $LOCATION; properties = @{} } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress | Set-Content body.json
az rest --method put --output none --body "@body.json" `
  --url "https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/$SUBSCRIPTION_ID/resourceGroups/$RG/providers/Microsoft.Web/connectorGateways/${GATEWAY}?api-version=2026-05-01-preview"
@{ location = $LOCATION; identity = @{ type = "SystemAssigned" }; properties = @{ publicNetworkAccess = "Enabled" } } |
  ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5 -Compress | Set-Content body.json
az rest --method put --output none --url "$GW`?$API" --body "@body.json"
```

### Deploy the model in Foundry

While the gateway provisions, create a Foundry account with a `gpt-6-luna` deployment. Then give the gateway's
managed identity the **Foundry User** role on the account. The gateway calls the model with this identity, so your
apps never hold a Foundry key.

```bash title="Bash"
az cognitiveservices account create --resource-group "$RG" --name "$FOUNDRY" --location "$LOCATION" \
  --kind AIServices --sku S0 --custom-domain "$FOUNDRY" --yes --output none
az cognitiveservices account deployment create --resource-group "$RG" --name "$FOUNDRY" \
  --deployment-name "$DEPLOYMENT" --model-name gpt-6-luna --model-version 2026-09-22 --model-format OpenAI \
  --sku-name GlobalStandard --sku-capacity 10 --output none

export FOUNDRY_ID="$(az cognitiveservices account show --resource-group "$RG" --name "$FOUNDRY" --query id --output tsv)"
PRINCIPAL_ID="$(az resource show --ids "$GATEWAY_ID" --query identity.principalId --output tsv)"
az role assignment create --assignee-object-id "$PRINCIPAL_ID" --assignee-principal-type ServicePrincipal \
  --role "53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d" --scope "$FOUNDRY_ID" --output none    # Foundry User
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
az cognitiveservices account create --resource-group $RG --name $FOUNDRY --location $LOCATION `
  --kind AIServices --sku S0 --custom-domain $FOUNDRY --yes --output none
az cognitiveservices account deployment create --resource-group $RG --name $FOUNDRY `
  --deployment-name $DEPLOYMENT --model-name gpt-6-luna --model-version 2026-09-22 --model-format OpenAI `
  --sku-name GlobalStandard --sku-capacity 10 --output none

$FOUNDRY_ID   = az cognitiveservices account show --resource-group $RG --name $FOUNDRY --query id --output tsv
$PRINCIPAL_ID = az resource show --ids $GATEWAY_ID --query identity.principalId --output tsv
az role assignment create --assignee-object-id $PRINCIPAL_ID --assignee-principal-type ServicePrincipal `
  --role "53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d" --scope $FOUNDRY_ID --output none    # Foundry User
```

### Publish the model

Wait for the gateway, then publish the deployment in three requests: a provider that points at the Foundry account
and signs in with the managed identity, a model for the deployment, and an alias that apps send in the `model` field.

```bash title="Bash"
az resource wait --ids "$GATEWAY_ID" --api-version 2025-09-01-preview --custom "properties.provisioningState=='Succeeded'"

az rest --method put --output none --url "$WS/modelProviders/$PROVIDER?$API" \
  --body "$(jq -cn --arg e "https://$FOUNDRY.cognitiveservices.azure.com/" --arg id "$FOUNDRY_ID" '{properties: {kind: "Foundry",
      foundry: {endpoint: $e, resourceIds: [$id], authentication: {kind: "ManagedIdentity",
        managedIdentity: {resource: "https://cognitiveservices.azure.com/"}}}}}')"
az rest --method put --output none --url "$WS/modelProviders/$PROVIDER/models/$DEPLOYMENT?$API" \
  --body "$(jq -cn --arg id "$FOUNDRY_ID/deployments/$DEPLOYMENT" --arg d "$DEPLOYMENT" '{properties: {
      apiFormat: "OpenAIChatCompletions", supportedEndpoints: ["/openai/v1/chat/completions", "/openai/v1/responses"],
      deployment: {resourceId: $id, modelName: $d}}}')"
az rest --method put --url "$WS/aliases/$DEPLOYMENT?$API" --query properties.aliasName --output tsv \
  --body "$(jq -cn --arg id "$GATEWAY_ID/workspaces/default/modelProviders/$PROVIDER/models/$DEPLOYMENT" \
      '{properties: {backendModels: [{resourceId: $id}]}}')"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
az resource wait --ids $GATEWAY_ID --api-version 2025-09-01-preview --custom "properties.provisioningState=='Succeeded'"

@{ properties = @{ kind = "Foundry"; foundry = @{
      endpoint       = "https://$FOUNDRY.cognitiveservices.azure.com/"
      resourceIds    = @($FOUNDRY_ID)
      authentication = @{ kind = "ManagedIdentity"; managedIdentity = @{ resource = "https://cognitiveservices.azure.com/" } } } } } |
  ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10 -Compress | Set-Content body.json
az rest --method put --output none --url "$WS/modelProviders/$PROVIDER`?$API" --body "@body.json"
@{ properties = @{
      apiFormat          = "OpenAIChatCompletions"
      supportedEndpoints = @("/openai/v1/chat/completions", "/openai/v1/responses")
      deployment         = @{ resourceId = "$FOUNDRY_ID/deployments/$DEPLOYMENT"; modelName = $DEPLOYMENT } } } |
  ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10 -Compress | Set-Content body.json
az rest --method put --output none --url "$WS/modelProviders/$PROVIDER/models/$DEPLOYMENT`?$API" --body "@body.json"
@{ properties = @{ backendModels = @(@{ resourceId = "$GATEWAY_ID/workspaces/default/modelProviders/$PROVIDER/models/$DEPLOYMENT" }) } } |
  ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10 -Compress | Set-Content body.json
az rest --method put --url "$WS/aliases/$DEPLOYMENT`?$API" --body "@body.json" --query properties.aliasName --output tsv
Remove-Item body.json
```

### Create a runtime API key

Create a key for your app. Then read the key, the gateway URL, and the alias into environment variables, so that
the key never shows on screen.

```bash title="Bash"
az rest --method put --output none --url "$GW/apiKeys/app-first-call?$API" --body '{"properties":{}}'

export AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY="$(az rest --method post --url "$GW/apiKeys/app-first-call/listSecrets?$API" \
  --query primaryKey --output tsv)"
export AI_GATEWAY_URL="https://$(az resource show --ids "$GATEWAY_ID" --query properties.frontend.defaultHostname --output tsv)"
export AI_GATEWAY_MODEL="$DEPLOYMENT"
echo "$AI_GATEWAY_URL"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
'{"properties":{}}' | Set-Content body.json
az rest --method put --output none --url "$GW/apiKeys/app-first-call?$API" --body "@body.json"
Remove-Item body.json

$env:AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY = az rest --method post --url "$GW/apiKeys/app-first-call/listSecrets?$API" `
  --query primaryKey --output tsv
$env:AI_GATEWAY_URL     = "https://" + (az resource show --ids $GATEWAY_ID --query properties.frontend.defaultHostname --output tsv)
$env:AI_GATEWAY_MODEL   = $DEPLOYMENT
$env:AI_GATEWAY_URL
```

> **Checkpoint:** the alias request printed `gpt-6-luna`, and the last command printed your gateway's runtime URL,
> for example `https://aigw-abc123.eastus2-01.ai.gateway.azure.com`.

### Make your first call

Send a Chat Completions request to the gateway's OpenAI-compatible base URL, the way an app does: the alias in the
`model` field and the key in the `api-key` header.

```bash title="Bash"
curl -sS "$AI_GATEWAY_URL/default/models/openai/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "api-key: $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"model\":\"$AI_GATEWAY_MODEL\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"In one sentence, what does an AI gateway do?\"}]}" \
  | jq -r '.choices[0].message.content // .error.message'
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$body = @{
  model    = $env:AI_GATEWAY_MODEL
  messages = @(@{ role = "user"; content = "In one sentence, what does an AI gateway do?" })
} | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5
$reply = Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post -Uri "$env:AI_GATEWAY_URL/default/models/openai/v1/chat/completions" `
  -Headers @{ "api-key" = $env:AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY } -ContentType "application/json" -Body $body
$reply.choices[0].message.content
```

> **Checkpoint:** the model answers in one sentence. Your gateway is live, and your app never needed a Foundry key:
> only the gateway's managed identity calls Foundry. If you get `403` or `404` in the first minute, the gateway's new
> role on the Foundry account is still taking effect. Wait a minute and run the call again.

To see what you created, open the [AI Gateway portal](https://ai.gateway.azure.com) and select your gateway in the top
bar: **Models**, **Access** › **Keys**, and the **Catalog** playground.

### Clean up

To keep exploring, skip this step: [lab 03](../03-multi-provider-aliases/README.md) and the labs after it work on this
gateway. On the labs site, save the resource group and the gateway name (`$RG` and `$GATEWAY`) in **Your values**.
Otherwise, delete the resource group, which holds the gateway and the Foundry account. Then purge the Foundry account:
deleted Foundry accounts stay soft-deleted for 48 hours and keep counting against your quota until you purge them.

```bash title="Bash"
az group delete --name "$RG" --yes
az cognitiveservices account purge --name "$FOUNDRY" --resource-group "$RG" --location "$LOCATION"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
az group delete --name $RG --yes
az cognitiveservices account purge --name $FOUNDRY --resource-group $RG --location $LOCATION
```

If Cloud Shell timed out, set `RG`, `FOUNDRY`, and `LOCATION` again with the names that you used: the suffix in
**Set your variables** is random.

> **Checkpoint:** `az group exists --name $RG` prints `false`.

<!-- track: iac | Bicep + azd -->

**What you need:** [Azure Cloud Shell](https://shell.azure.com), in Bash or PowerShell. It's already signed in and has
the Azure Developer CLI (`azd`), the Azure CLI, `curl`, `tar`, and `jq`. Locally,
[install azd](https://aka.ms/azd-install) and the Azure CLI, and sign in with `azd auth login` and `az login`. The
template creates the Foundry deployment for you.

### Download the template

The template is a small azd project: an `azure.yaml` and a Bicep file for each scope. The labs site serves it as one
archive, so you don't clone anything.

```bash title="Bash"
curl -fsSL https://azure.github.io/ai-gateway/labs/quickstart/aigw-quickstart.tar.gz | tar -xz
cd aigw-quickstart
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
Invoke-WebRequest https://azure.github.io/ai-gateway/labs/quickstart/aigw-quickstart.tar.gz -OutFile aigw-quickstart.tar.gz
tar -xzf aigw-quickstart.tar.gz; Remove-Item aigw-quickstart.tar.gz
Set-Location aigw-quickstart
```

`infra/main.bicep` creates the resource group `rg-<environment name>` and passes unique names to
`infra/resources.bicep`, which creates the five building blocks in the same order as the other tracks:

<!-- include: infra/resources.bicep -->

### Deploy with azd up

Create an azd environment named `aigw-quickstart` in your current subscription, so that azd doesn't prompt you. Then
provision everything with one command. It takes about three minutes.

```bash title="Bash"
azd env new aigw-quickstart --location eastus2 --subscription "$(az account show --query id --output tsv)"
azd up
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
azd env new aigw-quickstart --location eastus2 --subscription (az account show --query id --output tsv)
azd up
```

For Sweden Central, use `--location swedencentral`. azd saves the template's outputs, like the gateway URL and the
alias, as environment values. The API key isn't an output, so it never lands in a file or a deployment log.

### Read the URL, the alias, and the key

Read the outputs, and read the key from the gateway into an environment variable, so that it never shows on screen.

```bash title="Bash"
export AI_GATEWAY_URL="$(azd env get-value AI_GATEWAY_URL)"
export AI_GATEWAY_MODEL="$(azd env get-value AI_GATEWAY_MODEL)"
export AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY="$(az rest --method post --query primaryKey --output tsv \
  --url "https://management.azure.com$(azd env get-value AI_GATEWAY_ID)/apiKeys/app-first-call/listSecrets?api-version=2025-09-01-preview")"
echo "$AI_GATEWAY_URL"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$env:AI_GATEWAY_URL     = azd env get-value AI_GATEWAY_URL
$env:AI_GATEWAY_MODEL   = azd env get-value AI_GATEWAY_MODEL
$GATEWAY_ID             = azd env get-value AI_GATEWAY_ID
$env:AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY = az rest --method post --query primaryKey --output tsv `
  --url "https://management.azure.com$GATEWAY_ID/apiKeys/app-first-call/listSecrets?api-version=2025-09-01-preview"
$env:AI_GATEWAY_URL
```

> **Checkpoint:** `azd up` ended with `SUCCESS`, and the last command printed your gateway's runtime URL, for example
> `https://aigw-abc123.eastus2-01.ai.gateway.azure.com`.

### Make your first call

Send a Chat Completions request to the gateway's OpenAI-compatible base URL, the way an app does: the alias in the
`model` field and the key in the `api-key` header.

```bash title="Bash"
curl -sS "$AI_GATEWAY_URL/default/models/openai/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "api-key: $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"model\":\"$AI_GATEWAY_MODEL\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"In one sentence, what does an AI gateway do?\"}]}" \
  | jq -r '.choices[0].message.content // .error.message'
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$body = @{
  model    = $env:AI_GATEWAY_MODEL
  messages = @(@{ role = "user"; content = "In one sentence, what does an AI gateway do?" })
} | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5
$reply = Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post -Uri "$env:AI_GATEWAY_URL/default/models/openai/v1/chat/completions" `
  -Headers @{ "api-key" = $env:AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY } -ContentType "application/json" -Body $body
$reply.choices[0].message.content
```

> **Checkpoint:** the model answers in one sentence. Your gateway is live, and your app never needed a Foundry key:
> only the gateway's managed identity calls Foundry. If you get `403` or `404` in the first minute, the gateway's new
> role on the Foundry account is still taking effect. Wait a minute and run the call again.

To see what you created, open the [AI Gateway portal](https://ai.gateway.azure.com) and select your gateway in the top
bar: **Models**, **Access** › **Keys**, and the **Catalog** playground.

### Clean up

To keep exploring, skip this step: [lab 03](../03-multi-provider-aliases/README.md) and the labs after it work on this
gateway. Otherwise, in the `aigw-quickstart` folder, delete everything that `azd up` created. `--purge` also purges
the Foundry account, which would otherwise stay soft-deleted for 48 hours and keep counting against your quota. It
takes about ten minutes.

```bash title="Bash"
azd down --purge --force
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
azd down --purge --force
```

> **Checkpoint:** `azd down` ended with `SUCCESS`. The resource group `rg-aigw-quickstart` is gone, and you can delete
> the `aigw-quickstart` folder.

<!-- /tracks -->

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| A subscription is disabled in **Create AI gateway** | You can't write API Management or connector gateway resources in it | Pick another subscription, or ask for **Contributor** on it. |
| `AuthorizationFailed` on `Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments` | You can create resources but not role assignments | Ask for **Owner**, or **Role Based Access Control Administrator**, on the resource group. |
| `InsufficientQuota` on the model deployment | The subscription has no `gpt-6-luna` capacity left in the region | Start again in `swedencentral`: set `LOCATION` in the Azure CLI track, or run `azd env new` with a new name and `--location swedencentral` in the Bicep + azd track. Or free capacity in [Foundry](https://ai.azure.com). |
| `InvalidResourceGroupLocation` from `azd up` | The resource group `rg-<environment name>` already exists in another region | Run `azd env new` with a new environment name, or delete the old resource group. |
| `403` or `404` from the gateway in the first minute | The gateway's role on the Foundry account, or the new alias, is still taking effect | Wait a minute and call again. |
| `403` from the backend that doesn't go away | The gateway's managed identity has no role on the Foundry account | Assign it **Foundry User** on the account, as in the Azure CLI track's **Deploy the model in Foundry** step, and wait a few minutes. |
| `401` | The key is missing, wrong, or in the wrong header | Send it in the `api-key` header, or as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. In the portal, copy it again from **Access** › **Keys**. |
| `400` that mentions authentication | The request has both an `api-key` and an `Authorization` header | Send only one of them. |
| `The subscription is not registered to use namespace` | A resource provider isn't registered yet | Run the `az provider register` loop from **Start creating the gateway**, then try again. |

- [Publish models from any provider behind stable aliases](../03-multi-provider-aliases/README.md): put models from several providers behind names your apps keep.
- [Throttle tokens per caller with token limits](../06-token-limits/README.md): give every app its own allowance.

# How Azure AI Gateway works

Every team that ships generative AI hits the same questions. Which models may we call, and with which keys?
Who spent the tokens? How do we stop one agent from starving everyone else, or from calling a tool it should
never touch? The **AI Gateway tier** of Azure API Management answers them in one place: apps and agents call one
gateway, and the gateway decides who gets in, which model or tool answers, what each call may cost, and what gets
recorded.

<!-- video: media/walkthrough.mp4 | Narrated walkthrough: how Azure AI Gateway works (3 min) -->

![Azure AI Gateway architecture: clients call one gateway that routes to model providers and tool sources](../assets/diagrams/architecture.svg "Apps, agents, and coding agents call one gateway. The gateway authenticates them, applies policies, routes model calls through aliases, federates tools, and emits OpenTelemetry.")

> [!NOTE]
> The AI Gateway tier is in public preview in **East US 2** and **Sweden Central**. The gateway itself is free
> during the preview. Connected services, such as Microsoft Foundry inference and Application Insights, are billed
> normally.

## Before you begin

This lab is a guided reading. You don't need to deploy anything.

- If you already have a gateway, open the [AI Gateway portal](https://ai.gateway.azure.com) in another tab and
  follow the portal tour at the end.
- If you don't have one yet, read on. You create your first gateway in
  [Provision your first AI gateway](../01-provision-gateway/README.md).

## How it works

The gateway sits on the path of every model call and every tool call. It has two faces:

- **Data plane**: the runtime endpoints your code calls, at `https://<gateway>.eastus2-01.ai.gateway.azure.com`.
- **Control plane**: the product portal at [ai.gateway.azure.com](https://ai.gateway.azure.com) and the Azure
  Resource Manager API for the `Microsoft.ApiManagement/aigateways` resource type, which you call with
  `az rest`, Bicep, or any REST client.

| Building block | What it is | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Gateway** | An AI Gateway resource (`Microsoft.ApiManagement/aigateways`) in your subscription | `https://<gateway>.eastus2-01.ai.gateway.azure.com` |
| **Backend model** | A model at a provider, such as a Foundry deployment or an Anthropic model | `gpt-6-luna` at Microsoft Foundry |
| **Alias** | The stable, gateway-wide name clients send in the `model` field | `chat` |
| **MCP server** | One governed MCP endpoint that federates tools from one or more sources | `/default/toolservers/<server-name>/mcp` |
| **Policy** | A rule on the gateway or on one asset: limits, budgets, safety, filters | Token rate limit, Cost limit |
| **Access** | How callers authenticate: API keys or Microsoft Entra ID roles | `api-key` header or Entra token |
| **Managed identity** | How the gateway authenticates to backends | Foundry User role on the Foundry account |
| **Monitoring** | OpenTelemetry metrics, logs, and traces for every call | Application Insights or any OTLP endpoint |

Model calls use protocols developers already know. The OpenAI-compatible base URL is
`https://<gateway-host>/default/models/openai/v1` (append `/responses` or `/chat/completions`), and
Anthropic Messages lives at `/default/models/anthropic/v1/messages`. The gateway passes requests through without
translating between OpenAI and Anthropic formats, so call each model on an interface it advertises.

## Follow one request

Press **Play** to send a request through the gateway. Then switch scenarios to see where each policy stops a
request and which status code the caller gets back.

<!-- widget: request-lifecycle -->

![Request lifecycle through the gateway](../assets/diagrams/request-lifecycle.svg "Every applicable policy is evaluated before the gateway forwards a request. If one blocks it, the backend is never called.")

Three rules explain almost every response you'll see in these labs:

1. **Policies run before the backend.** If any applicable policy blocks a request, the gateway answers right away
   and never calls the backend.
2. **Each block has a predictable status.** `401` for missing or invalid credentials, `403` for IP filters and
   cost limits (`LlmCostQuotaExceeded`), `429` with `Retry-After` for token and request rate limits, and `400` for
   content safety.
3. **Everything is recorded.** Allowed and blocked calls both show up in **Monitoring**, along with the policies
   that affected them.

## Models and aliases

A **backend model** is what a provider serves. An **alias** is what your clients call. Microsoft Foundry imports
create an alias for each model by default, and you can add more. Because clients only know the alias, you can move
it to a newer or cheaper model without a code change, and the alias keeps its own policies.

<!-- widget: alias-retarget -->

![Aliases decouple clients from backend models](../assets/diagrams/aliases.svg "Two aliases can share one backend model with different policies. Retargeting an alias needs no client change.")

You can put models from Microsoft Foundry, Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and
custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints behind aliases. You try it in
[Route models from several providers behind aliases](../03-multi-provider-aliases/README.md).

## MCP servers and tools

Agents need tools as much as models. An **MCP server** on the gateway gives agents one endpoint and one credential
for tools from remote MCP servers, OpenAPI specifications, built-in connectors, and Foundry Toolbox. Tool names are
namespaced per source, and **tool availability** decides which tools clients can see and call.

![MCP tool federation](../assets/diagrams/mcp-federation.svg "One MCP endpoint federates tools from several sources. Tool availability and policies apply to every call.")

## Policies and scopes

You add a policy at **gateway scope**, where it applies to every compatible asset including assets you add later,
or to **individual assets**: a backend model, an alias, or an MCP server. Pick an asset below to see every policy
that applies to it.

<!-- widget: policy-layers -->

| Policy | Applies to | When it blocks |
|---|---|---|
| **Token rate limit** | Models and aliases | `429` with `Retry-After` |
| **Request rate limit** | Models, aliases, and MCP servers | `429` with `Retry-After` |
| **Cost limit** | Models and aliases | `403` `LlmCostQuotaExceeded` |
| **Content safety** | Models, aliases, and MCP servers | `400` |
| **IP filter** | Models, aliases, and MCP servers | `403` |
| **Agent 365 tool threat protection** | MCP servers | Denies the tool call |

At gateway scope, the policy type decides which assets are relevant. A gateway-scope cost limit, for example,
tracks one budget across all models.

## Identities on both sides

The gateway separates **who is calling** from **how the gateway reaches the backend**. Callers use an API key or a
Microsoft Entra token with one of the AI Gateway data-plane roles. The gateway uses its own managed identity, or a
provider key it stores, to call backends. Callers never see backend credentials.

![Identity boundaries](../assets/diagrams/identity-boundaries.svg "Inbound and outbound identities are authorized separately.")

## Observability

The gateway emits OpenTelemetry metrics, logs, and traces for model calls, tool calls, and policy decisions. Send
them to Application Insights to light up the built-in **Monitoring** dashboard, or to any OTLP endpoint.

![Observability with OpenTelemetry](../assets/diagrams/observability.svg "Signals flow to Application Insights, which powers the Monitoring dashboard, or to any OTLP endpoint.")

## Take a portal tour

If you have a gateway, walk through the portal now. Otherwise, use the screenshots and come back after
[lab 01](../01-provision-gateway/README.md).

<!-- steps -->

### Open your gateway

Go to [ai.gateway.azure.com](https://ai.gateway.azure.com) and sign in. Use the gateway switcher in the top bar to
pick a gateway. The left rail lists **Home**, **Catalog**, **Models**, **MCP servers**, **Access**, **Policies**,
**Monitoring**, **Networking**, and **Managed identities**. Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>K</kbd> to open the
command palette from anywhere.

### Browse models and aliases

Select **Models**. Each backend model lists its provider and the aliases that point to it.

![Models page with aliases](../assets/screens/models-aliases.png "Models: backend models and the aliases clients call.")

### Look at an MCP server

Select **MCP servers** and open a server. The tool availability settings decide which tools clients can see.

![MCP server tool availability](../assets/screens/mcp-tool-controls.png "MCP servers: tool availability with exact lists and name patterns.")

### Start a policy

Select **Policies** › **Add policy**. The wizard asks for a **Type**, then a **Scope** (**Gateway** or
**Individual assets**), then the settings. Close the wizard without saving.

![Add policy wizard](../assets/screens/policy-add-wizard.png "Policies: pick a type, a scope, then configure.")

### Open Monitoring

Select **Monitoring**. When Application Insights is connected, the **Overview**, **Models**, **Tools**,
**Policies**, and **Traces** tabs show live traffic.

![Monitoring overview](../assets/screens/monitoring-overview.png "Monitoring: requests, outcomes, tokens, and estimated cost.")

<!-- /steps -->

## Verify

Check your understanding before you move on.

<details>
<summary>An app sends <code>"model": "chat"</code>. What must <code>chat</code> be?</summary>

A callable **alias** on the gateway. The `model` field must exactly match an alias, not a provider deployment name.
</details>

<details>
<summary>A caller exceeds a token rate limit. Is the backend called?</summary>

No. The gateway answers `429 Too Many Requests` with `Retry-After` and never forwards the request.
</details>

<details>
<summary>You add an IP filter at gateway scope, then add a new model next week. Is the new model protected?</summary>

Yes. Gateway-scope policies apply to every compatible asset, including assets you add later.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Which credential does the gateway use to call a Microsoft Foundry model?</summary>

Its own managed identity, which needs the **Foundry User** role on the Foundry account. The caller's key or token
is never forwarded.
</details>

> **Checkpoint**
> You can explain the request lifecycle, the difference between a backend model and an alias, and where gateway
> and asset policies apply.

## Clean up

Nothing to clean up. This lab doesn't create resources.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| A model call says the model can't be found | The `model` field doesn't match an alias | Copy the alias from **Models**, or from the code sample in **Catalog** |
| An Anthropic call fails on the OpenAI endpoint | The gateway doesn't translate between protocols | Call `/default/models/anthropic/v1/messages` with `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01` |
| You can't create a gateway in your region | The preview runs in two regions | Use East US 2 or Sweden Central |
| Monitoring is empty | No telemetry destination | Connect Application Insights in **Monitoring** › **Settings** |

progress is saved in this browser.

# Provision your AI Gateway

Your platform team is about to put every model and tool that the company's apps and agents use behind one
governed entry point. Before anyone can publish a model, issue a key, or set a budget, you need the gateway
itself. In this lab you create a shared AI Gateway, find its runtime URL and managed identity, and learn your
way around the portal so you're ready for the rest of the labs.

<!-- video: media/walkthrough.mp4 | Narrated walkthrough: create an AI Gateway in the portal and tour it (3 min) -->

![What provisioning creates: you choose a name, resource group, and region; Azure creates the connector gateway, the AI Gateway, and its managed identity; you get a runtime URL, a default workspace, and the portal](../assets/diagrams/provisioning.svg "One gateway per environment is the usual starting point. Every later lab publishes models, tools, keys, and policies on it.")

## Before you begin

- An Azure subscription with access to the AI Gateway preview. The AI Gateway tier is free during public
  preview. Connected services, such as Foundry inference and Application Insights, are billed normally.
- Permission to create the gateway, for example **Contributor** on the resource group, or on the subscription
  if you create a new resource group. Creating a gateway needs write access to both API Management and
  connector gateways.
- For the portal track: a browser and your Azure account.
- For the CLI and IaC tracks: the [Azure CLI](https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/install-azure-cli) 2.75 or
  later, signed in with `az login`, plus `jq` for the Bash snippets. The CLI track calls the Azure Resource
  Manager REST API with `az rest`, because the `az aigateway` extension doesn't manage the new `aigateways`
  resource type yet.
- Recommended reading: [How AI Gateway works](../00-how-ai-gateway-works/README.md).

Set these variables once. Every track and the **Verify** section reuse them.

```bash title="Bash"
az account set --subscription "<subscription-id>"

export RG="<resource-group>"               # for example rg-ai-gateway-labs
export GATEWAY="<gateway>"                 # globally unique, 24 characters or fewer, part of the runtime URL
export LOCATION="<location>"               # eastus2 or swedencentral
export SUBSCRIPTION_ID="$(az account show --query id -o tsv)"
export GATEWAY_ID="/subscriptions/$SUBSCRIPTION_ID/resourceGroups/$RG/providers/Microsoft.ApiManagement/aigateways/$GATEWAY"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
az account set --subscription "<subscription-id>"

$RG              = "<resource-group>"      # for example rg-ai-gateway-labs
$GATEWAY         = "<gateway>"             # globally unique, 24 characters or fewer, part of the runtime URL
$LOCATION        = "<location>"            # eastus2 or swedencentral
$SUBSCRIPTION_ID = az account show --query id -o tsv
$GATEWAY_ID      = "/subscriptions/$SUBSCRIPTION_ID/resourceGroups/$RG/providers/Microsoft.ApiManagement/aigateways/$GATEWAY"
```

> [!IMPORTANT]
> During public preview, AI Gateway is available in **East US 2** (`eastus2`) and **Sweden Central**
> (`swedencentral`). Create the resource group in one of these regions so that defaults line up. The gateway
> name must be 1–24 characters: letters, digits, and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen.

## How it works

An AI Gateway is an Azure Resource Manager resource of type `Microsoft.ApiManagement/aigateways`. You manage it
in the [AI Gateway portal](https://ai.gateway.azure.com), which is separate from the Azure portal, or through
Azure Resource Manager with the CLI, REST, or Bicep. Each gateway has a companion connector gateway
(`Microsoft.Web/connectorGateways`) with the same name, which is created first. The service sets the SKU and
capacity itself, so the only real decisions are the name, the region, and the resource group.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Resource type | `Microsoft.ApiManagement/aigateways` (API version `2025-09-01-preview`), plus `Microsoft.Web/connectorGateways` with the same name |
| Regions (preview) | East US 2 (`eastus2`), Sweden Central (`swedencentral`) |
| Name | 1–24 characters: letters, digits, and hyphens. It becomes the first label of the runtime host name |
| Runtime URL | `https://` + `properties.frontend.defaultHostname`, for example `https://<gateway>.eastus2-01.ai.gateway.azure.com` |
| Runtime routes | Models under `/default/models/…`, MCP servers under `/default/toolservers/<server>/mcp` |
| Outbound identity | A system-assigned managed identity, used to call Foundry and other Microsoft Entra–protected backends |
| Provisioning time | A few minutes, often less |

Everything you publish later lives in the gateway's `default` workspace. That's why every runtime route
starts with `/default/`. Applications authenticate **inbound** with an API key or a Microsoft Entra token. The
gateway authenticates **outbound** to each backend, usually with its managed identity, so apps never hold
provider credentials.

![AI Gateway architecture: apps and agents call one gateway that governs models and tools](../assets/diagrams/architecture.svg "Apps and agents call one runtime URL. The gateway applies access, policies, and telemetry before it routes to models and MCP servers.")

## Create the gateway

Pick one track. Each track produces the same result: a gateway named `<gateway>` in `<resource-group>`, with a
system-assigned managed identity.

<!-- track: portal | Portal -->

### Sign in to the AI Gateway portal

Open the [AI Gateway portal](https://ai.gateway.azure.com) and sign in with your Azure account. If this is your
first gateway, the portal takes you straight into gateway creation. If you already have a gateway, open the
gateway switcher in the top bar and start creating a new one from there.

### Enter the gateway details

In **Create AI gateway**, enter a globally unique **Name** of 24 characters or fewer, or select
**Generate a new name**. Then choose the subscription, a **Resource group** (**New** or **Existing**), and the
**Region** (**East US 2** or **Sweden Central**). Under **Advanced**, keep
**Enable system-assigned managed identity** selected, **Public network access** set to **Enabled**, and
**Public routing**. **Private routing** connects the gateway to private backends through a virtual network and
can only be chosen at creation. [Lab 18](../18-private-networking/README.md) covers it.

![What to choose in Create AI gateway: a unique name, a subscription, a resource group, and a preview region, with the Advanced defaults kept](../assets/diagrams/create-gateway.svg "Fill in the basics, keep the Advanced defaults, then select Create gateway.")

> [!NOTE]
> The subscription picker lists every subscription you can see. Subscriptions where you lack write permission
> for API Management and connector gateways are disabled, and the portal explains why.

### Watch it provision

Select **Create gateway**. The portal shows provisioning progress in place, and a new gateway is typically ready
in a few minutes.

### Open the setup guide on Home

When provisioning finishes, **Home** opens with a setup guide for publishing models, adding MCP servers, and
creating runtime access. Leave it for now. You publish your first model in the next lab, and the guide stays
on **Home** until you finish it.

> **Checkpoint**
> The gateway switcher in the top bar shows `<gateway>`, and **Home** shows the setup guide.

<!-- track: cli | Azure CLI -->

### Register the resource providers

The gateway lives in the `Microsoft.ApiManagement` resource provider and its connector gateway in
`Microsoft.Web`. Registering is a one-time step per subscription, and it returns quickly when a provider is
already registered.

```bash
az provider register -n Microsoft.ApiManagement --wait
az provider register -n Microsoft.Web --wait
```

### Create a resource group

```bash
az group create --name "$RG" --location "$LOCATION"
```

### Create the connector gateway

Every AI gateway has a companion `Microsoft.Web/connectorGateways` resource with the same name. The portal and
the Bicep template create it first, so do the same.

```bash title="Bash"
az rest --method put \
  --url "https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/$SUBSCRIPTION_ID/resourceGroups/$RG/providers/Microsoft.Web/connectorGateways/$GATEWAY?api-version=2026-05-01-preview" \
  --body "$(jq -cn --arg location "$LOCATION" '{location: $location, properties: {}}')"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
@{ location = $LOCATION; properties = @{} } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress | Set-Content body.json
az rest --method put `
  --url "https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/$SUBSCRIPTION_ID/resourceGroups/$RG/providers/Microsoft.Web/connectorGateways/${GATEWAY}?api-version=2026-05-01-preview" `
  --body "@body.json"
```

### Start creating the gateway

The request body only needs the region, a system-assigned managed identity, and public network access. There's
no SKU, capacity, or publisher to set: the service picks them. Azure accepts the request and provisioning
continues in the background.

```bash title="Bash"
az rest --method put --url "https://management.azure.com$GATEWAY_ID?api-version=2025-09-01-preview" \
  --body "$(jq -cn --arg location "$LOCATION" \
    '{location: $location, identity: {type: "SystemAssigned"}, properties: {publicNetworkAccess: "Enabled"}}')"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
@{
  location   = $LOCATION
  identity   = @{ type = "SystemAssigned" }
  properties = @{ publicNetworkAccess = "Enabled" }
} | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5 -Compress | Set-Content body.json
az rest --method put --url "https://management.azure.com${GATEWAY_ID}?api-version=2025-09-01-preview" --body "@body.json"
Remove-Item body.json
```

### Wait for provisioning

```bash title="Bash"
az resource wait --ids "$GATEWAY_ID" --api-version 2025-09-01-preview \
  --custom "properties.provisioningState=='Succeeded'"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
az resource wait --ids $GATEWAY_ID --api-version 2025-09-01-preview `
  --custom "properties.provisioningState=='Succeeded'"
```

The command returns when `provisioningState` reaches `Succeeded`, usually within a few minutes.

### Read the runtime URL and identity

```bash title="Bash"
az resource show --ids "$GATEWAY_ID" \
  --query "{name:name, location:location, state:properties.provisioningState, host:properties.frontend.defaultHostname, principalId:identity.principalId}" \
  -o table
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
az resource show --ids $GATEWAY_ID `
  --query "{name:name, location:location, state:properties.provisioningState, host:properties.frontend.defaultHostname, principalId:identity.principalId}" `
  -o table
```

> **Checkpoint**
> The table shows `Succeeded`, a `Host` like `<gateway>.eastus2-01.ai.gateway.azure.com`, and a `PrincipalId`
> GUID.

<!-- track: iac | Bicep -->

### Review the template

The template creates what the portal creates: a `Microsoft.Web/connectorGateways` resource first, then the AI
gateway (`Microsoft.ApiManagement/aigateways`) with the same name, a system-assigned identity, and public
network access enabled. There's no SKU, capacity, or publisher to set. Keep both resources together in your own
templates.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| `gatewayName` | Required. The gateway name, 24 characters or fewer |
| `location` | `eastus2` (default) or `swedencentral` |
| `tags` | Optional. Tags applied to both resources |
| `backendSubnetId` | Optional. A subnet for outbound virtual network integration, which can only be set at creation. See [Lab 18](../18-private-networking/README.md) |

<!-- include: infra/main.bicep -->

On GitHub, open [infra/main.bicep](infra/main.bicep).

### Create a resource group

```bash
az group create --name "$RG" --location "$LOCATION"
```

### Deploy the template

Run the deployment from the lab folder. The template defaults `location` to `eastus2`, so pass your region
explicitly.

```bash title="Bash"
az deployment group create -g "$RG" \
  --template-file infra/main.bicep \
  --parameters gatewayName="$GATEWAY" location="$LOCATION" \
  --query properties.outputs
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
az deployment group create -g $RG `
  --template-file infra/main.bicep `
  --parameters gatewayName=$GATEWAY location=$LOCATION `
  --query properties.outputs
```

Expected output (trimmed):

```json
{
  "connectorGatewayId": { "type": "String", "value": "/subscriptions/<subscription-id>/resourceGroups/<resource-group>/providers/Microsoft.Web/connectorGateways/<gateway>" },
  "gatewayId":   { "type": "String", "value": "/subscriptions/<subscription-id>/resourceGroups/<resource-group>/providers/Microsoft.ApiManagement/aigateways/<gateway>" },
  "gatewayName": { "type": "String", "value": "<gateway>" },
  "gatewayUrl":  { "type": "String", "value": "https://<gateway>.eastus2-01.ai.gateway.azure.com" },
  "principalId": { "type": "String", "value": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000" }
}
```

> [!TIP]
> `BCP081` warnings about `Microsoft.ApiManagement/aigateways` and `Microsoft.Web/connectorGateways` mean that
> Bicep has no local type definitions for these preview resources. They don't block the deployment.

> **Checkpoint**
> The deployment succeeds and the outputs show `gatewayUrl` and `principalId`.

<!-- /tracks -->

## Verify

<!-- steps -->

### Call the runtime URL

Read the host name from the gateway rather than building it yourself, then send a request without a key. Any
HTTP status proves that DNS, TLS, and the gateway are up. A new gateway with no models answers `404`; after you
add a model and a key in the next lab, a call without a key gets `400` or `401`.

```bash title="Bash"
export AI_GATEWAY_URL="https://$(az resource show --ids "$GATEWAY_ID" --query properties.frontend.defaultHostname -o tsv)"
echo "$AI_GATEWAY_URL"

curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" "${AI_GATEWAY_URL%/}/default/models/openai/v1/chat/completions"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$env:AI_GATEWAY_URL = "https://$(az resource show --ids $GATEWAY_ID --query properties.frontend.defaultHostname -o tsv)"
$env:AI_GATEWAY_URL

(Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "$($env:AI_GATEWAY_URL.TrimEnd('/'))/default/models/openai/v1/chat/completions" `
  -SkipHttpErrorCheck).StatusCode
```

A `Could not resolve host` error means the gateway isn't ready yet. Wait a minute and try again.

### Find the gateway on Home

Open the [AI Gateway portal](https://ai.gateway.azure.com). If you created the gateway with the CLI or Bicep,
select it in the gateway switcher in the top bar. **Home** shows the setup guide for your new gateway.

### Check the managed identity

Select **Managed identities**. On the **Configure identities** tab, the system-assigned identity is enabled.
Its principal ID matches `principalId` from the CLI or Bicep output. In later labs you grant this identity
access to Foundry so that the gateway can call your models without keys.

![The Managed identities page with the system-assigned identity enabled](../assets/screens/managed-identities.png "Managed identities › Configure identities shows the system-assigned identity with its principal ID and tenant ID. You can add user-assigned identities here too.")

### Tour the portal

Use the left navigation to get familiar with each area. You visit most of them in later labs.

| Area | What you do there | Where you learn it |
|---|---|---|
| **Home** | Follow the setup guide for models, MCP servers, and runtime access | This lab |
| **Catalog** | Browse published models and MCP servers, try them in the playground, and copy endpoints and code samples | [Lab 02](../02-first-model-call/README.md) |
| **Access** | Create runtime API keys on the **Keys** tab and grant Microsoft Entra roles on the **Entra ID** tab | [Lab 10](../10-api-keys/README.md), [Lab 11](../11-entra-rbac/README.md) |
| **Models** | Import Foundry deployments, add custom models from other providers, and manage aliases | [Lab 02](../02-first-model-call/README.md), [Lab 03](../03-multi-provider-aliases/README.md) |
| **MCP servers** | Publish MCP servers and control which tools are available | [Lab 04](../04-federate-mcp-tools/README.md), [Lab 05](../05-mcp-tool-controls/README.md) |
| **Policies** | Add token and request rate limits, cost limits, content safety, and IP filters at gateway or asset scope | [Lab 06](../06-token-limits/README.md), [Lab 09](../09-gateway-baselines/README.md) |
| **Monitoring** | Send telemetry to an OTLP destination and use the built-in dashboard and traces | [Lab 13](../13-monitoring/README.md) |
| **Networking** | Review network access and outbound virtual network integration | [Lab 18](../18-private-networking/README.md) |
| **Managed identities** | Manage the identities that the gateway uses to call backends | [Lab 12](../12-backend-identity/README.md) |

The top bar holds the gateway switcher, **What's new**, notifications, and a command palette (Ctrl+K) to jump
to any page.

> [!NOTE]
> Some portal versions show **Keys** directly in the left navigation instead of **Access** › **Keys**. Both
> lead to the same runtime API keys.

<!-- /steps -->

> **Checkpoint**
> The runtime URL answers with an HTTP status, the gateway appears on **Home**, and **Managed identities**
> shows the system-assigned identity enabled.

## Go further

- **One gateway per environment.** Repeat the IaC track with a different `gatewayName` for dev, test, and
  production, and keep the template in source control next to your app.
- **Tag for ownership and chargeback.** The template's `tags` parameter applies the same tags to the gateway
  and its connector gateway, so set them when you create each environment's gateway:

  ```bash
  az deployment group create -g "$RG" --template-file infra/main.bicep \
    --parameters gatewayName="$GATEWAY" location="$LOCATION" \
                 tags='{"workload":"ai-gateway-labs","owner":"platform-team","costCenter":"1234"}'
  ```
- **Use a user-assigned identity.** When several gateways must share one backend identity, add a
  user-assigned identity on **Managed identities**. See
  [Call backends with managed identities](../12-backend-identity/README.md).

## Clean up

The gateway is free during preview, and every later lab reuses it. **Keep it** until you finish the labs you
plan to do.

When you're done with all the labs, delete the resource group. That removes the gateway, its connector gateway,
and everything else in the group. The command asks for confirmation.

```bash title="Bash"
az group delete --name "$RG"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
az group delete --name $RG
```

To keep the resource group, delete the AI gateway first and then its connector gateway. Deleting the gateway
also deletes everything you published on it.

```bash title="Bash"
az resource delete --ids "$GATEWAY_ID" --api-version 2025-09-01-preview
az resource delete -g "$RG" -n "$GATEWAY" --resource-type Microsoft.Web/connectorGateways --api-version 2026-05-01-preview
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
az resource delete --ids $GATEWAY_ID --api-version 2025-09-01-preview
az resource delete -g $RG -n $GATEWAY --resource-type Microsoft.Web/connectorGateways --api-version 2026-05-01-preview
```

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Your subscription is disabled in the portal's subscription picker | You lack write permission for API Management or connector gateways in that subscription | Ask for **Contributor** on the subscription or resource group, or pick another subscription. |
| The deployment fails because the region isn't supported | `$LOCATION` or the template's `location` is outside the preview regions | Use `eastus2` or `swedencentral`. The template accepts only these two values and defaults to `eastus2`. |
| The name is rejected | Gateway names are globally unique and limited to 24 characters: letters, digits, and hyphens, starting with a letter | Pick another name that follows the rules. |
| `MissingSubscriptionRegistration` | A resource provider isn't registered in the subscription | Run `az provider register -n Microsoft.ApiManagement --wait` and `az provider register -n Microsoft.Web --wait`, or ask your subscription administrator. |
| `Could not resolve host` when you call the URL | Provisioning or DNS isn't finished | Run the `az resource wait` command from the CLI track and retry. |
| `az aigateway` commands can't find your gateway | The `aigateway` CLI extension doesn't manage the new `aigateways` resource type yet | Use `az rest` and `az resource` as shown in this lab. |

- [How AI Gateway works](../00-how-ai-gateway-works/README.md): the concepts behind models, tools, policies, and identity.
- Docs: [Configure AI Gateway in the portal](https://ai.gateway.azure.com/docs/quickstarts/portal) and
  [AI Gateway CLI quickstart](https://ai.gateway.azure.com/docs/quickstarts/cli).
