# Publish a Foundry model and make your first call

The first product team wants to use `gpt-6-luna`, which already runs in your Microsoft Foundry account. You
don't want to hand every team the Foundry endpoint and a provider key. In this lab you publish the deployment
through your gateway, give the team a runtime API key of its own, and make the first call from the playground,
a shell, and code. The gateway authenticates to Foundry with its own managed identity, so the app never sees a
Foundry credential.

![A request travels from the app through the gateway to the model and back](../assets/diagrams/request-lifecycle.svg "The gateway checks the caller's key, applies policies, calls the backend with its own identity, and records telemetry on the way back.")

## Before you begin

- Complete [Provision your AI Gateway](../01-provision-gateway/README.md). You need the gateway, its resource
  group, and its runtime URL.
- A model deployment in a Microsoft Foundry (Azure AI Services) or Azure OpenAI account, for example
  `gpt-6-luna`. If you don't have one, deploy the optional template described below.
- Permission to grant the gateway access to the account: **Owner**, **User Access Administrator**, or **Role
  Based Access Control Administrator** on the Foundry account. You also need to change the gateway, for example
  **Contributor** on its resource group.
- For the CLI and IaC tracks: the [Azure CLI](https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/install-azure-cli) 2.75 or
  later, signed in with `az login`, plus `jq` for the Bash snippets. The CLI track calls the Azure Resource
  Manager REST API with `az rest`, because the `az aigateway` extension doesn't manage the new `aigateways`
  resource type yet.
- For the code track: Python 3.9 or later, Node.js 22.18 or later, or the .NET 8 SDK.

Set these variables once. Every track and the **Verify** section reuse them.

```bash title="Bash"
export RG="<resource-group>"
export GATEWAY="<gateway>"
export FOUNDRY_RG="<foundry-resource-group>"      # resource group of the Foundry account
export FOUNDRY_ACCOUNT="<foundry-account-name>"   # the account name, not a project or deployment name
export DEPLOYMENT="gpt-6-luna"                    # the model deployment to publish
export PROVIDER="foundry-models"                  # CLI and IaC tracks: the gateway provider to create

export API="api-version=2025-09-01-preview"
export GATEWAY_ID="$(az resource show -g "$RG" -n "$GATEWAY" --resource-type Microsoft.ApiManagement/aigateways --query id -o tsv)"
export GW="https://management.azure.com$GATEWAY_ID"
export WS="$GW/workspaces/default"
export AI_GATEWAY_URL="https://$(az resource show --ids "$GATEWAY_ID" --query properties.frontend.defaultHostname -o tsv)"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$RG              = "<resource-group>"
$GATEWAY         = "<gateway>"
$FOUNDRY_RG      = "<foundry-resource-group>"     # resource group of the Foundry account
$FOUNDRY_ACCOUNT = "<foundry-account-name>"       # the account name, not a project or deployment name
$DEPLOYMENT      = "gpt-6-luna"                   # the model deployment to publish
$PROVIDER        = "foundry-models"               # CLI and IaC tracks: the gateway provider to create

$API        = "api-version=2025-09-01-preview"
$GATEWAY_ID = az resource show -g $RG -n $GATEWAY --resource-type Microsoft.ApiManagement/aigateways --query id -o tsv
$GW         = "https://management.azure.com$GATEWAY_ID"
$WS         = "$GW/workspaces/default"
$env:AI_GATEWAY_URL = "https://$(az resource show --ids $GATEWAY_ID --query properties.frontend.defaultHostname -o tsv)"
```

<details>
<summary>No Foundry deployment yet? Create one with Bicep.</summary>

[infra/foundry.bicep](infra/foundry.bicep) creates an Azure AI Services account with a `gpt-6-luna`
`GlobalStandard` deployment, mirroring the reference sample. Pick a region where the model is available. Model
inference is billed per use.

```bash
az group create --name "$FOUNDRY_RG" --location eastus2
az deployment group create -g "$FOUNDRY_RG" \
  --template-file infra/foundry.bicep \
  --parameters accountName="$FOUNDRY_ACCOUNT" deploymentName="$DEPLOYMENT" \
  --query properties.outputs.deploymentId.value -o tsv
```

</details>

## How it works

Publishing a model has three parts. A **model provider** tells the gateway where the Foundry account is and
how to authenticate to it. A **backend model** registers one deployment under that provider. A callable
**alias** is the stable name that clients send in the request `model` field. Importing from Foundry creates all
three for you.

Clients call one runtime URL with a gateway API key. The gateway validates the key before anything else, runs
the policies that apply, swaps the caller's key for its own managed identity token, and forwards the request
unchanged to Foundry. The response comes back as is, and the gateway records token usage for monitoring.

| Step | What happens | Where you set it |
|---|---|---|
| Inbound authentication | An active runtime key in the `api-key` header, or as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` (what the OpenAI SDKs send), or the call fails with `401` | **Access** › **Keys** |
| Routing | `/default/models/openai/v1/chat/completions` or `/responses`, and `model` must equal an alias | Model details and its **Aliases** tab |
| Policies | Token limits, cost limits, and content safety run before the backend call | **Policies** (labs 06–09) |
| Backend authentication | The gateway's managed identity, with the **Foundry User** role on the account | Model provider |
| Telemetry | Tokens, latency, and the API key that made the call | **Monitoring** (lab 13) |

<!-- widget: request-lifecycle -->

## Publish the model and create a key

Pick one track. Each track publishes the deployment, gives you a callable alias, and creates a runtime API key.

<!-- track: portal | Portal -->

### Import the deployment from Foundry

1. Open the [AI Gateway portal](https://ai.gateway.azure.com) and select your gateway in the top bar.
2. Select **Models** › **Add** › **Models from Microsoft Foundry**. (On **Home**, **Add from Microsoft Foundry** in
   the **Set up your gateway** guide starts the same import.)
3. Select the subscription and resource group of your Foundry account. The wizard discovers the deployments
   automatically. Deployments that are already in this gateway can't be selected again.
4. Select the `gpt-6-luna` deployment and keep **Managed identity** as the **Authentication method**.
5. Under **Aliases**, keep **Create an alias for each model** selected, then select **Add models**.

> [!NOTE]
> The gateway calls Foundry with its system-assigned managed identity, which needs the **Foundry User** role on
> the account. If your first call returns `403` from the backend, assign the role yourself and wait a few
> minutes for it to take effect:
>
> ```bash
> PRINCIPAL_ID="$(az resource show --ids "$GATEWAY_ID" --query identity.principalId -o tsv)"
> FOUNDRY_ID="$(az cognitiveservices account show -g "$FOUNDRY_RG" -n "$FOUNDRY_ACCOUNT" --query id -o tsv)"
> az role assignment create --assignee-object-id "$PRINCIPAL_ID" --assignee-principal-type ServicePrincipal \
>   --role "53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d" --scope "$FOUNDRY_ID"
> ```

### Copy the callable alias

Open the imported model on **Models**. The model details show its base URL and supported interfaces, such as
**OpenAI Chat Completions** and **OpenAI Responses**. Open the **Aliases** tab and copy the alias exactly as
shown, then save it in your shell. Portal imports usually name it after the provider and the deployment, for
example `<foundry-account-name>/gpt-6-luna`.

```bash title="Bash"
export AI_GATEWAY_MODEL="<model-name>"    # the alias from the Aliases tab
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$env:AI_GATEWAY_MODEL = "<model-name>"    # the alias from the Aliases tab
```

### Create a runtime API key

1. Select **Access** › **Keys** › **Create API key**. Some portal versions show **Keys** directly in the left
   navigation.
2. In **Key name**, enter a name for the app that will use it, for example `app-first-call`, and select
   **Create**.
3. Copy the value from **API key created successfully**, for example with **Copy & done**. Copy it now: treat
   the value as shown only once.
4. Paste it into your shell without echoing it or writing it to a file:

```bash title="Bash"
read -rsp "AI Gateway API key: " AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY && export AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY && echo
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$env:AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY = Read-Host "AI Gateway API key" -MaskInput
```

> **Checkpoint**
> **Models** lists the Foundry deployment, its **Aliases** tab shows an alias, and **Access** › **Keys** shows
> `app-first-call`.

<!-- track: cli | Azure CLI -->

### Look up the Foundry account

Use the account name and resource group to look up its resource ID and endpoint. No need to copy a long ID from
the portal.

```bash title="Bash"
export FOUNDRY_ID="$(az cognitiveservices account show -g "$FOUNDRY_RG" -n "$FOUNDRY_ACCOUNT" --query id -o tsv)"
FOUNDRY_ENDPOINT="$(az cognitiveservices account show -g "$FOUNDRY_RG" -n "$FOUNDRY_ACCOUNT" --query properties.endpoint -o tsv)"
export FOUNDRY_ENDPOINT="${FOUNDRY_ENDPOINT%/}/"    # the provider expects a trailing slash
echo "$FOUNDRY_ID"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$FOUNDRY_ID       = az cognitiveservices account show -g $FOUNDRY_RG -n $FOUNDRY_ACCOUNT --query id -o tsv
$FOUNDRY_ENDPOINT = (az cognitiveservices account show -g $FOUNDRY_RG -n $FOUNDRY_ACCOUNT --query properties.endpoint -o tsv).TrimEnd('/') + '/'
$FOUNDRY_ID
```

### Grant the gateway access to the account

The portal import does three things for you: it grants the gateway's identity access to the account, creates the
provider, and registers the deployments. With the REST API, you do each step yourself. First, give the gateway's
system-assigned identity the **Foundry User** role on the account.

```bash title="Bash"
PRINCIPAL_ID="$(az resource show --ids "$GATEWAY_ID" --query identity.principalId -o tsv)"
az role assignment create --assignee-object-id "$PRINCIPAL_ID" --assignee-principal-type ServicePrincipal \
  --role "53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d" --scope "$FOUNDRY_ID" --query id -o tsv    # Foundry User
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$PRINCIPAL_ID = az resource show --ids $GATEWAY_ID --query identity.principalId -o tsv
az role assignment create --assignee-object-id $PRINCIPAL_ID --assignee-principal-type ServicePrincipal `
  --role "53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d" --scope $FOUNDRY_ID --query id -o tsv    # Foundry User
```

### Create the Foundry provider

The provider tells the gateway where the account is and to authenticate with its managed identity.

```bash title="Bash"
az rest --method put --url "$WS/modelProviders/$PROVIDER?$API" \
  --body "$(jq -cn --arg endpoint "$FOUNDRY_ENDPOINT" --arg id "$FOUNDRY_ID" '{properties: {
      kind: "Foundry", displayName: "Foundry models",
      foundry: {endpoint: $endpoint, resourceIds: [$id],
                authentication: {kind: "ManagedIdentity",
                                 managedIdentity: {resource: "https://cognitiveservices.azure.com/"}}}}}')" \
  --query "{name:name, kind:properties.kind, endpoint:properties.foundry.endpoint}"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
@{ properties = @{
    kind        = "Foundry"
    displayName = "Foundry models"
    foundry     = @{
      endpoint       = $FOUNDRY_ENDPOINT
      resourceIds    = @($FOUNDRY_ID)
      authentication = @{ kind = "ManagedIdentity"; managedIdentity = @{ resource = "https://cognitiveservices.azure.com/" } }
    }
  } } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10 -Compress | Set-Content body.json
az rest --method put --url "$WS/modelProviders/$PROVIDER`?$API" --body "@body.json" `
  --query "{name:name, kind:properties.kind, endpoint:properties.foundry.endpoint}"
```

### Register the deployment

A backend model registers one deployment under the provider. Name it after the deployment.

```bash title="Bash"
az rest --method put --url "$WS/modelProviders/$PROVIDER/models/$DEPLOYMENT?$API" \
  --body "$(jq -cn --arg id "$FOUNDRY_ID/deployments/$DEPLOYMENT" --arg d "$DEPLOYMENT" '{properties: {
      displayName: $d, apiFormat: "OpenAIChatCompletions",
      supportedEndpoints: ["/openai/v1/chat/completions", "/openai/v1/responses"],
      deployment: {resourceId: $id, modelName: $d}}}')" \
  --query "{name:name, deployment:properties.deployment.modelName}"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
@{ properties = @{
    displayName        = $DEPLOYMENT
    apiFormat          = "OpenAIChatCompletions"
    supportedEndpoints = @("/openai/v1/chat/completions", "/openai/v1/responses")
    deployment         = @{ resourceId = "$FOUNDRY_ID/deployments/$DEPLOYMENT"; modelName = $DEPLOYMENT }
  } } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10 -Compress | Set-Content body.json
az rest --method put --url "$WS/modelProviders/$PROVIDER/models/$DEPLOYMENT`?$API" --body "@body.json" `
  --query "{name:name, deployment:properties.deployment.modelName}"
```

To publish more deployments, repeat this step and the next one for each name that
`az cognitiveservices account deployment list -g "$FOUNDRY_RG" -n "$FOUNDRY_ACCOUNT" --query "[].name" -o tsv`
returns.

### Publish an alias

Clients send an alias in the request `model` field, not the backend model name. Publish one named after the
deployment that points at the model you registered.

```bash title="Bash"
export AI_GATEWAY_MODEL="$DEPLOYMENT"
MODEL_ID="$GATEWAY_ID/workspaces/default/modelProviders/$PROVIDER/models/$DEPLOYMENT"
az rest --method put --url "$WS/aliases/$AI_GATEWAY_MODEL?$API" \
  --body "$(jq -cn --arg id "$MODEL_ID" '{properties: {backendModels: [{resourceId: $id}]}}')" \
  --query "{alias:properties.aliasName, target:properties.backendModels[0].resourceId}"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$env:AI_GATEWAY_MODEL = $DEPLOYMENT
$MODEL_ID = "$GATEWAY_ID/workspaces/default/modelProviders/$PROVIDER/models/$DEPLOYMENT"
@{ properties = @{ backendModels = @(@{ resourceId = $MODEL_ID }) } } |
  ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10 -Compress | Set-Content body.json
az rest --method put --url "$WS/aliases/$($env:AI_GATEWAY_MODEL)?$API" --body "@body.json" `
  --query "{alias:properties.aliasName, target:properties.backendModels[0].resourceId}"
Remove-Item body.json
```

### Create a runtime API key

The PUT returns metadata only. Read the generated value with `listSecrets` straight into a variable so it never
appears on screen.

```bash title="Bash"
az rest --method put --url "$GW/apiKeys/app-first-call?$API" --body '{"properties":{}}' \
  --query "{name:name, state:properties.state}"

AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY="$(az rest --method post --url "$GW/apiKeys/app-first-call/listSecrets?$API" \
  --query primaryKey -o tsv)" && export AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
'{"properties":{}}' | Set-Content body.json
az rest --method put --url "$GW/apiKeys/app-first-call?$API" --body "@body.json" `
  --query "{name:name, state:properties.state}"
Remove-Item body.json

$env:AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY = az rest --method post --url "$GW/apiKeys/app-first-call/listSecrets?$API" `
  --query primaryKey -o tsv
```

> **Checkpoint**
> `az rest --url "$WS/models?$API" --query "value[].{name:name, provider:properties.providerKind}" -o table`
> lists your deployment with the provider `Foundry`, the alias request returned your model's ID as `target`, and
> `az rest --url "$GW/apiKeys?$API" --query "value[].{name:name, state:properties.state}" -o table` shows
> `app-first-call` as `active`.

<!-- track: iac | Bicep -->

### Review the template

The template adds to the gateway from lab 01. It grants the gateway's identity the **Foundry User** role on the
account (in the account's own resource group), creates a Foundry model provider that authenticates with the
managed identity, registers the deployment as a backend model with a per-caller token limit, publishes an alias,
and creates a runtime API key.

<!-- include: infra/main.bicep -->

On GitHub, open [infra/main.bicep](infra/main.bicep) and [infra/foundry-user-role.bicep](infra/foundry-user-role.bicep).

### Deploy the template

Run the deployment from the lab folder. The alias defaults to the deployment name.

```bash title="Bash"
FOUNDRY_ID="$(az cognitiveservices account show -g "$FOUNDRY_RG" -n "$FOUNDRY_ACCOUNT" --query id -o tsv)"

az deployment group create -g "$RG" \
  --template-file infra/main.bicep \
  --parameters gatewayName="$GATEWAY" foundryAccountId="$FOUNDRY_ID" \
               deploymentName="$DEPLOYMENT" providerName="$PROVIDER" \
  --query properties.outputs
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$FOUNDRY_ID = az cognitiveservices account show -g $FOUNDRY_RG -n $FOUNDRY_ACCOUNT --query id -o tsv

az deployment group create -g $RG `
  --template-file infra/main.bicep `
  --parameters gatewayName=$GATEWAY foundryAccountId=$FOUNDRY_ID `
               deploymentName=$DEPLOYMENT providerName=$PROVIDER `
  --query properties.outputs
```

The outputs include `aliasName`, `apiKeyName`, and `modelEndpoint`.

### Read the alias and key

Template outputs never contain the key value. Read it with the `listSecrets` action straight into a variable.

```bash title="Bash"
export AI_GATEWAY_MODEL="$DEPLOYMENT"    # the aliasName output
AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY="$(az rest --method post --url "$GW/apiKeys/app-first-call/listSecrets?$API" \
  --query primaryKey -o tsv)" && export AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$env:AI_GATEWAY_MODEL = $DEPLOYMENT      # the aliasName output
$env:AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY = az rest --method post --url "$GW/apiKeys/app-first-call/listSecrets?$API" `
  --query primaryKey -o tsv
```

> **Checkpoint**
> The deployment succeeds, and its outputs show `providerName`, `modelName`, and `aliasName`.

<!-- /tracks -->

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Role assignments can take a few minutes to take effect. Until then, calls can fail with `403` from the
> backend. Wait and retry.

## Make your first call

Use the same alias and key everywhere. The gateway exposes the OpenAI-compatible base URL
`<gateway URL>/default/models/openai/v1`, so OpenAI SDKs only need a different base URL and the runtime key.

<!-- track: portal | Playground -->

### Try the model in Catalog

1. Select **Catalog** and pick your model.
2. Send a prompt in the built-in playground, for example `Write a one-sentence status update.`
3. Copy the endpoint and the code samples (cURL, PowerShell 7+, Python, TypeScript, and .NET) for your app.

> [!TIP]
> If the playground asks you to **Sign in again**, your portal session expired. Sign in and resend the prompt.

<!-- track: cli | curl and PowerShell -->

### Call Chat Completions

```bash title="Bash"
curl -sS "${AI_GATEWAY_URL%/}/default/models/openai/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "api-key: $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"model\":\"$AI_GATEWAY_MODEL\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Write a one-sentence status update.\"}]}" \
  | jq -r '.choices[0].message.content'
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$body = @{
  model    = $env:AI_GATEWAY_MODEL
  messages = @(@{ role = "user"; content = "Write a one-sentence status update." })
} | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5

$reply = Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post `
  -Uri "$($env:AI_GATEWAY_URL.TrimEnd('/'))/default/models/openai/v1/chat/completions" `
  -Headers @{ "api-key" = $env:AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY } -ContentType "application/json" -Body $body
$reply.choices[0].message.content
```

### Call the Responses API

```bash title="Bash"
curl -sS "${AI_GATEWAY_URL%/}/default/models/openai/v1/responses" \
  -H "api-key: $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"model\":\"$AI_GATEWAY_MODEL\",\"input\":\"Summarize what an AI gateway does in one sentence.\"}" \
  | jq -r '[.output[] | select(.type == "message") | .content[] | select(.type == "output_text") | .text] | join("")'
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$body = @{ model = $env:AI_GATEWAY_MODEL; input = "Summarize what an AI gateway does in one sentence." } |
  ConvertTo-Json

$reply = Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post `
  -Uri "$($env:AI_GATEWAY_URL.TrimEnd('/'))/default/models/openai/v1/responses" `
  -Headers @{ "api-key" = $env:AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY } -ContentType "application/json" -Body $body
($reply.output | Where-Object type -eq "message").content.text -join ""
```

### Run both calls with a script

The script prints the HTTP status and the reply for each interface, which makes failures easier to read.

<!-- include: infra/call-model.sh -->

On GitHub, open [infra/call-model.sh](infra/call-model.sh) or [infra/call-model.ps1](infra/call-model.ps1).

```bash title="Bash"
./infra/call-model.sh
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
./infra/call-model.ps1
```

<!-- track: code | Code -->

### Install the SDK

Each sample reads `AI_GATEWAY_URL`, `AI_GATEWAY_MODEL`, and `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` from the environment, so the
key never lives in code. Run the commands from the lab folder.

```bash title="Python"
cd infra
pip install -r requirements.txt     # the openai package
```

```bash title="TypeScript"
cd infra
npm install                         # the openai npm package
```

```bash title="C#"
cd infra/dotnet
dotnet restore                      # no extra packages: HttpClient and System.Text.Json
```

### Call the model from code

The OpenAI SDKs send their API key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, which the model endpoint accepts, so the
runtime key goes straight into the SDK. Don't also add an `api-key` default header: the gateway rejects a request
that has both with `400`. The .NET sample uses `HttpClient`, like the .NET samples in the AI Gateway docs, so it
sends the `api-key` header explicitly.

```python title="Python"
import os

from openai import OpenAI

gateway_url = os.environ["AI_GATEWAY_URL"].rstrip("/")
model = os.environ["AI_GATEWAY_MODEL"]

client = OpenAI(
    base_url=f"{gateway_url}/default/models/openai/v1",
    api_key=os.environ["AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY"],
)

response = client.responses.create(model=model, input="Write a one-sentence status update.")
print(f"Responses API:    {response.output_text}")

completion = client.chat.completions.create(
    model=model,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Describe an AI gateway in one sentence."}],
)
print(f"Chat Completions: {completion.choices[0].message.content}")
```

```typescript title="TypeScript"
import OpenAI from "openai";

const gatewayUrl = process.env.AI_GATEWAY_URL!.replace(/\/+$/, "");
const model = process.env.AI_GATEWAY_MODEL!;

const client = new OpenAI({
  baseURL: `${gatewayUrl}/default/models/openai/v1`,
  apiKey: process.env.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY!,
});

const response = await client.responses.create({ model, input: "Write a one-sentence status update." });
console.log(`Responses API:    ${response.output_text}`);

const completion = await client.chat.completions.create({
  model,
  messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Describe an AI gateway in one sentence." }],
});
console.log(`Chat Completions: ${completion.choices[0].message.content}`);
```

```csharp title="C#"
using System.Net.Http.Json;
using System.Text.Json;

var gatewayUrl = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("AI_GATEWAY_URL")!.TrimEnd('/');
var model = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("AI_GATEWAY_MODEL")!;

using var http = new HttpClient { BaseAddress = new Uri($"{gatewayUrl}/default/models/openai/v1/") };
http.DefaultRequestHeaders.Add("api-key", Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY"));

using var reply = await http.PostAsJsonAsync("chat/completions", new
{
    model,
    messages = new[] { new { role = "user", content = "Describe an AI gateway in one sentence." } },
});
reply.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();
using var json = JsonDocument.Parse(await reply.Content.ReadAsStringAsync());
Console.WriteLine(json.RootElement.GetProperty("choices")[0].GetProperty("message").GetProperty("content").GetString());
```

The full samples in `infra` also call the Responses API from C# and print token usage: open
[first-call.py](infra/first-call.py), [first-call.ts](infra/first-call.ts), and
[dotnet/Program.cs](infra/dotnet/Program.cs).

### Run the sample

```bash title="Python"
python first-call.py
```

```bash title="TypeScript"
node first-call.ts      # Node.js 22.18 or later; on older versions run: npx tsx first-call.ts
```

```bash title="C#"
dotnet run
```

Expected output (your text differs):

```text
Responses API:    All systems are running normally and the release is on track for Friday.
Chat Completions: An AI gateway is a governed entry point that routes, secures, and observes calls to AI models and tools.
```

> **Checkpoint**
> The model answers through the gateway, and you never used a Foundry key or endpoint.

## Verify

<!-- steps -->

### Confirm the model is published

```bash title="Bash"
az rest --url "$WS/models?$API" --query "value[].{name:name, provider:properties.providerKind}" -o table
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
az rest --url "$WS/models?$API" --query "value[].{name:name, provider:properties.providerKind}" -o table
```

The list includes your deployment. In the portal, **Catalog** lists the model too.

### Get a 200 with the key

```bash title="Bash"
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" "${AI_GATEWAY_URL%/}/default/models/openai/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "api-key: $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"model\":\"$AI_GATEWAY_MODEL\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"ping\"}]}"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$body = @{ model = $env:AI_GATEWAY_MODEL; messages = @(@{ role = "user"; content = "ping" }) } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5
(Invoke-WebRequest -Method Post -Uri "$($env:AI_GATEWAY_URL.TrimEnd('/'))/default/models/openai/v1/chat/completions" `
  -Headers @{ "api-key" = $env:AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY } -ContentType "application/json" -Body $body -SkipHttpErrorCheck).StatusCode
```

Expect `HTTP 200`.

### Get a 401 without the key

Send the same request without the `api-key` header. The gateway rejects it before any policy runs or the
backend is called.

```bash title="Bash"
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" "${AI_GATEWAY_URL%/}/default/models/openai/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"model\":\"$AI_GATEWAY_MODEL\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"ping\"}]}"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
(Invoke-WebRequest -Method Post -Uri "$($env:AI_GATEWAY_URL.TrimEnd('/'))/default/models/openai/v1/chat/completions" `
  -ContentType "application/json" -Body $body -SkipHttpErrorCheck).StatusCode
```

Expect `HTTP 401`.

### Check that the alias is what clients call

Change one character in `model` and resend the request with the key. The call fails with `404` and
`model_not_found` because `model` must match an alias exactly. Backend model names and Foundry deployment names
aren't callable unless an alias with that name exists.

<!-- /steps -->

> **Checkpoint**
> You got `200` with the key, `401` without it, and an error for a name that isn't an alias.

## Go further

- **Publish more deployments.** After you add deployments in Foundry, rerun the portal import, or repeat the
  CLI track's **Register the deployment** and **Publish an alias** steps for each new deployment.
- **Add a per-caller token limit.** The Bicep track already sets `tokensPerMinute`. Learn how limits behave in
  [Throttle tokens per caller with token limits](../06-token-limits/README.md).
- **Publish models from other providers.** Put OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, or Google Vertex AI models behind
  the same gateway in [Publish models from any provider behind stable aliases](../03-multi-provider-aliases/README.md).

## Clean up

Keep the gateway, model, alias, and key. The next labs reuse them.

When you're done with the labs, delete the key, the alias, and the provider, then remove the role assignment that
the gateway received on the Foundry account. Delete the alias first: deleting the provider also deletes its
models, but not the aliases that point at them. Deleting a model from the gateway doesn't delete the Foundry
deployment. The commands use the names from the CLI and IaC tracks. If you imported in the portal, use the
provider and alias names shown on **Models**.

```bash title="Bash"
az rest --method delete --url "$GW/apiKeys/app-first-call?$API"
az rest --method delete --url "$WS/aliases/$DEPLOYMENT?$API"
az rest --method delete --url "$WS/modelProviders/$PROVIDER?$API"

PRINCIPAL_ID="$(az resource show --ids "$GATEWAY_ID" --query identity.principalId -o tsv)"
FOUNDRY_ID="$(az cognitiveservices account show -g "$FOUNDRY_RG" -n "$FOUNDRY_ACCOUNT" --query id -o tsv)"
az role assignment delete --assignee "$PRINCIPAL_ID" --role "53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d" --scope "$FOUNDRY_ID"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
az rest --method delete --url "$GW/apiKeys/app-first-call?$API"
az rest --method delete --url "$WS/aliases/$DEPLOYMENT`?$API"
az rest --method delete --url "$WS/modelProviders/$PROVIDER`?$API"

$PRINCIPAL_ID = az resource show --ids $GATEWAY_ID --query identity.principalId -o tsv
$FOUNDRY_ID = az cognitiveservices account show -g $FOUNDRY_RG -n $FOUNDRY_ACCOUNT --query id -o tsv
az role assignment delete --assignee $PRINCIPAL_ID --role "53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d" --scope $FOUNDRY_ID
```

If you created the Foundry account with `infra/foundry.bicep`, delete its resource group with
`az group delete --name "$FOUNDRY_RG"`.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `401` from the gateway | The key is missing, misspelled, or deleted | Send an active runtime key in the `api-key` header or as the SDK API key. Create a new key if you lost the value. |
| `400` with `Specify either an API key or an Authorization header, not both` | The client sends an `api-key` header and an `Authorization` header, such as an SDK placeholder key | Pass the runtime key as the SDK API key and remove the `api-key` default header. |
| `403` mentioning permissions on the Foundry account | The gateway's identity lacks **Foundry User**, or the assignment hasn't propagated yet | Wait a few minutes. If it persists, assign the role as shown in the portal track. |
| `404` with `model_not_found` | `model` doesn't match an alias exactly | Copy the alias from the model's **Aliases** tab or from **Catalog**. |
| `400` `unsupported_parameter` for `max_tokens` or `temperature` | `gpt-6-luna` is a reasoning model | Send `max_completion_tokens` instead of `max_tokens`. Set `temperature` only together with `reasoning_effort: "none"`. |
| `200` with empty `content` and `finish_reason` `length` | Reasoning used the whole `max_completion_tokens` budget | Raise the budget, or send `reasoning_effort: "none"` for short, direct replies. |
| The Responses API call fails while Chat Completions works | The model doesn't advertise the Responses interface | Check the supported interfaces on the model details page and call only those. |
| The import wizard doesn't list your account | It's already imported into this gateway, or you can't read it in that subscription | Check **Models** for an existing provider, or ask for read access to the account. |
| `AuthorizationFailed` on `roleAssignments` during deployment | You can't create role assignments on the Foundry account | Ask for **Role Based Access Control Administrator** on the account, or have an owner grant the role. |

# Publish models from any provider behind stable aliases

The support team wants to try Claude, and the batch team wants the same model for nightly summaries. You don't
want either team to hold an Anthropic key, and you don't want to edit their code every time you switch models.
In this lab you add Anthropic as a provider whose key only the gateway knows, publish two Claude models behind
aliases such as `support-chat`, and then point `support-chat` at a bigger model while the clients keep sending
the same name.

![Clients call an alias, and the alias points to a backend model of a provider](../assets/diagrams/aliases.svg "An alias is the stable name in the request's model field. You can point it at a different backend model at any time.")

<!-- widget: alias-retarget {"alias":"team-chat","targets":[{"provider":"Microsoft Foundry","model":"gpt-6-luna","note":"Lower cost","logo":"microsoft-foundry"},{"provider":"Microsoft Foundry","model":"gpt-6.1-sol","note":"Higher quality","logo":"microsoft-foundry"},{"provider":"OpenAI","model":"gpt-6-luna","note":"Custom provider","logo":"openai"}]} -->

## Before you begin

- Complete [Publish a Foundry model and make your first call](../02-first-model-call/README.md). You need the
  gateway, a runtime API key, and the Foundry alias you created there.
- An API key from the [Claude Console](https://console.anthropic.com) that can call two models, for example
  `claude-haiku-5-5` and `claude-sonnet-5-5`. To use another provider instead, see the values in
  [Add Anthropic as a custom provider](#add-anthropic-as-a-custom-provider).
- Permission to change the gateway, for example **Contributor** on its resource group.
- For the REST track and the **Verify** scripts: the
  [Azure CLI](https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/install-azure-cli) 2.75 or later, signed in with `az login`.
  The Bash scripts also use `jq`; the PowerShell scripts need PowerShell 7 or later.

Set these variables once. Every track and the **Verify** section reuse them.

```bash title="Bash"
export RG="<resource-group>"
export GATEWAY="<gateway>"
export PROVIDER="anthropic"               # the gateway provider you create in this lab
export FAST_MODEL="claude-haiku-5-5"      # two models that your Anthropic key can call
export SMART_MODEL="claude-sonnet-5-5"

export API="api-version=2025-09-01-preview"
export GATEWAY_ID="$(az resource show -g "$RG" -n "$GATEWAY" --resource-type Microsoft.ApiManagement/aigateways --query id -o tsv)"
export GW="https://management.azure.com$GATEWAY_ID"
export WS="$GW/workspaces/default"
export AI_GATEWAY_URL="https://$(az resource show --ids "$GATEWAY_ID" --query properties.frontend.defaultHostname -o tsv)"
# Paste the gateway runtime key from lab 02, not the Anthropic key. Don't commit it or write it to a file.
read -rsp "AI Gateway API key: " AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY && export AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY && echo
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$RG          = "<resource-group>"
$GATEWAY     = "<gateway>"
$PROVIDER    = "anthropic"                # the gateway provider you create in this lab
$FAST_MODEL  = "claude-haiku-5-5"         # two models that your Anthropic key can call
$SMART_MODEL = "claude-sonnet-5-5"

$API         = "api-version=2025-09-01-preview"
$GATEWAY_ID  = az resource show -g $RG -n $GATEWAY --resource-type Microsoft.ApiManagement/aigateways --query id -o tsv
$GW          = "https://management.azure.com$GATEWAY_ID"
$WS          = "$GW/workspaces/default"
$env:AI_GATEWAY_URL = "https://$(az resource show --ids $GATEWAY_ID --query properties.frontend.defaultHostname -o tsv)"
# Paste the gateway runtime key from lab 02, not the Anthropic key. Don't commit it or write it to a file.
$env:AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY = Read-Host "AI Gateway API key" -MaskInput
```

## How it works

The gateway publishes models in three layers:

| Object | What it holds | Unique within | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Model provider** | A backend endpoint and the credential the gateway uses to call it | The gateway | `anthropic`, key sent in `x-api-key` |
| **Backend model** | A model that the provider serves, and the interfaces it supports | Its provider | `claude-haiku-5-5` |
| **Alias** | The callable name that clients put in the `model` field. It points to one or more backend models and can carry its own policies. | The gateway | `support-chat` |

Clients only ever see the gateway URL, their runtime key, and the alias. The provider key stays in the gateway.
In this lab each alias points to one backend model. To split traffic across several backend models by priority
and weight, see [Route an alias across models by priority and weight](../22-model-routing/README.md).

Each interface has its own route under `https://<gateway>.eastus2-01.ai.gateway.azure.com/default/models`:

| Interface | Route |
|---|---|
| OpenAI Chat Completions | `/openai/v1/chat/completions` |
| OpenAI Responses | `/openai/v1/responses` |
| Anthropic Messages | `/anthropic/v1/messages` |

Every model runs in passthrough mode. The gateway keeps the provider's request and response format and doesn't
translate between OpenAI and Anthropic, so call each model on an interface it advertises, and retarget an
alias only to a model that supports the same interface.

## Add Anthropic as a custom provider

The gateway connects to these providers. Microsoft Foundry and Azure OpenAI can use the gateway's managed
identity. Every other provider is a custom provider, and the gateway stores its API key.

| | Provider | How you add it | Gateway authenticates with |
|---|---|---|---|
| <img src="../assets/providers/microsoft-foundry.png" alt="" height="24"> | Microsoft Foundry | **Models from Microsoft Foundry** | Managed identity (recommended) or API key |
| <img src="../assets/providers/azure-openai.png" alt="" height="24"> | Azure OpenAI | **Models from Microsoft Foundry** | Managed identity (recommended) or API key |
| <img src="../assets/providers/openai.png" alt="" height="24"> | OpenAI | **Models from a custom provider** | API key |
| <img src="../assets/providers/anthropic.png" alt="" height="24"> | Anthropic | **Models from a custom provider** | API key |
| <img src="../assets/providers/aws-bedrock.png" alt="" height="24"> | AWS Bedrock | **Models from a custom provider** | API key |
| <img src="../assets/providers/google-vertex.png" alt="" height="24"> | Google Vertex AI | **Models from a custom provider** | API key |
| <img src="../assets/providers/custom-models.png" alt="" height="24"> | Any other OpenAI-compatible endpoint | **Models from a custom provider** | API key |

Pick one track. Both tracks create the same result: a provider named `anthropic`, two backend models, and two
aliases. `support-chat` points to the fast model, and `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` points to the bigger one.

<!-- track: portal | Portal -->

### Start the custom provider wizard

Open the [AI Gateway portal](https://ai.gateway.azure.com) and select your gateway from the gateway switcher.
Select **Models** › **Add** › **Models from a custom provider**. **Add custom provider** in the
**Set up your gateway** guide on **Home** opens the same wizard.

On the **Provider** step, select **Create new provider** and fill in **Basic info**:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Display name** | `Anthropic` |
| **Provider name** | `anthropic` (used in the resource ID; you can't change it later) |
| **Description** | Optional |

Select **Next**.

### Connect the endpoint

On the **Endpoint** step, fill in **Endpoint and authentication**:

| Field | Value for Anthropic |
|---|---|
| **Base endpoint URL** | `https://api.anthropic.com` |
| **Header name** | `x-api-key` |
| **API key** | Your Anthropic API key |
| **Authentication scheme** | Leave **Include Bearer in the authorization header value** cleared. Anthropic expects the raw key. |

The wizard lists the provider's models by calling `<base endpoint URL>/v1/models`, so leave `/v1` off the base
URL. The key is stored in the gateway. Apps that call the gateway never receive it.

For other providers, change these values:

| Provider | Base endpoint URL | Header name | Authentication scheme |
|---|---|---|---|
| OpenAI | `https://api.openai.com` | `Authorization` | Selected, so the gateway sends `Bearer <key>` |
| Other OpenAI-compatible endpoints | The URL in front of `/v1/...` | The header the endpoint expects | As the endpoint expects |
| AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI | The provider's OpenAI-compatible endpoint, without the `/v1/...` path | The header that the provider's API key goes in | As the provider expects |

Select **Next**.

### Choose the models and their aliases

The **Models** step shows **Discovering available models…** while it calls the provider. Then select **Add** ›
**Individual model** and add each model:

| Field | First model | Second model |
|---|---|---|
| **Backend model** | `claude-haiku-5-5` | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
| **Supported endpoints** | **Anthropic messages** | **Anthropic messages** |
| **Callable alias** | Change it to `support-chat` | Keep the default, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` |

If discovery fails or times out, you can still add the models by hand. Select **Add models**.

> **Checkpoint**
> **Models** lists the two Claude models of the `Anthropic` provider and the aliases `support-chat` and
> `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`. Open a model: its **Overview** shows the Anthropic Messages endpoint,
> `https://<gateway>.eastus2-01.ai.gateway.azure.com/default/models/anthropic/v1/messages`.

<!-- track: rest | REST API -->

### Set the REST variables

The provider, its models, and the aliases are child resources of the gateway's `default` workspace. You set
`WS` (the workspace URL) and `API` in [Before you begin](#before-you-begin). Check that they point at your
gateway by listing its model providers. The command is the same in Bash and PowerShell.

```bash
az rest --url "$WS/modelProviders?$API" --query "value[].{name:name,kind:properties.kind}" -o table
```

The table lists the provider from lab 02, of kind `Foundry`. If the command fails, set the variables again.

### Create the provider

The request reads the Anthropic key from a hidden prompt, so it never lands in your shell history.

```bash title="Bash"
read -rsp "Anthropic API key: " ANTHROPIC_API_KEY && echo
az rest --method put --url "$WS/modelProviders/$PROVIDER?$API" \
  --body "$(jq -cn --arg key "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" '{properties: {
      kind: "Custom", displayName: "Anthropic",
      custom: {endpoint: "https://api.anthropic.com",
               authentication: {kind: "ApiKey", apiKey: {headerName: "x-api-key", value: $key}}}}}')" \
  --query "{name:name,kind:properties.kind,endpoint:properties.custom.endpoint}"
unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$key = Read-Host "Anthropic API key" -MaskInput
@{ properties = @{
    kind        = 'Custom'
    displayName = 'Anthropic'
    custom      = @{
      endpoint       = 'https://api.anthropic.com'
      authentication = @{ kind = 'ApiKey'; apiKey = @{ headerName = 'x-api-key'; value = $key } }
    }
  } } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10 -Compress | Set-Content -Path provider.json
az rest --method put --url "$WS/modelProviders/$PROVIDER`?$API" --body '@provider.json' `
  --query "{name:name,kind:properties.kind,endpoint:properties.custom.endpoint}"
Remove-Item provider.json; Remove-Variable key   # the file held the key, so delete it right away
```

For OpenAI, use `https://api.openai.com`, the header `Authorization`, and the value `Bearer <key>`.

### Register the backend models

The resource name of a backend model in the URL may only contain lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens. If the
provider's model ID contains other characters, replace them with `-` in the URL and keep the real ID in
`deployment.modelName`.

```bash title="Bash"
for MODEL in "$FAST_MODEL" "$SMART_MODEL"; do
  az rest --method put --url "$WS/modelProviders/$PROVIDER/models/$MODEL?$API" \
    --body "$(jq -cn --arg m "$MODEL" \
      '{properties: {displayName: $m, supportedEndpoints: ["/v1/messages"], deployment: {modelName: $m}}}')" \
    --query "{name:name,endpoints:properties.supportedEndpoints}" -o json
done
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
foreach ($model in $FAST_MODEL, $SMART_MODEL) {
  @{ properties = @{ displayName = $model; supportedEndpoints = @('/v1/messages'); deployment = @{ modelName = $model } } } |
    ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10 -Compress | Set-Content -Path model.json
  az rest --method put --url "$WS/modelProviders/$PROVIDER/models/$model`?$API" --body '@model.json' `
    --query "{name:name,endpoints:properties.supportedEndpoints}" -o json
}
Remove-Item model.json
```

> [!NOTE]
> The provider and model bodies mirror what the portal sends during the preview. For custom providers, `supportedEndpoints`
> holds the provider path: `/v1/messages` for Anthropic, `/v1/chat/completions` or `/v1/responses` for
> OpenAI-compatible endpoints. The model has no `apiFormat`. If the service rejects either request, create the
> provider and models with the **Portal** tab, then continue here with the aliases.

### Create the aliases

An alias lists its backend models by resource ID in `properties.backendModels`. Here each alias has one. The
callable name goes in `properties.aliasName`. Callable
names may contain `/`, but resource names can't, so the script derives the resource name the same way the
portal does: `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` is stored as `anthropic-claude-sonnet-5-5`.

```bash title="Bash"
./infra/alias.sh put support-chat "$PROVIDER" "$FAST_MODEL"
./infra/alias.sh put "$PROVIDER/$SMART_MODEL" "$PROVIDER" "$SMART_MODEL"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
./infra/alias.ps1 -ResourceGroup $RG -Gateway $GATEWAY put support-chat $PROVIDER $FAST_MODEL
./infra/alias.ps1 -ResourceGroup $RG -Gateway $GATEWAY put "$PROVIDER/$SMART_MODEL" $PROVIDER $SMART_MODEL
```

On GitHub, open [alias.sh](infra/alias.sh) or [alias.ps1](infra/alias.ps1). Each `put` sends a request like this:

```text
PUT .../workspaces/default/aliases/support-chat?api-version=2025-09-01-preview
{
  "properties": {
    "aliasName": "support-chat",
    "backendModels": [ { "resourceId": ".../workspaces/default/modelProviders/anthropic/models/claude-haiku-5-5" } ],
    "policies": []
  }
}
```

> **Checkpoint**
> `./infra/alias.sh list` shows `support-chat` → `anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5` and
> `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` → `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`, next to your Foundry alias from lab 02.

<!-- /tracks -->

## Call Claude through the gateway

Send a native Anthropic Messages request to the gateway's Anthropic route. Three things differ from a direct
call to Anthropic: the URL is the gateway's, the `api-key` header carries your gateway runtime key, and `model`
is the alias. Keep the `anthropic-version` header that the Messages API expects.

```bash title="Bash"
curl -sS "${AI_GATEWAY_URL%/}/default/models/anthropic/v1/messages" \
  -H "api-key: $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "support-chat", "max_tokens": 1024,
       "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "In one sentence, what is an AI gateway?"}]}' \
  | jq '{model, text: ([.content[] | select(.type == "text") | .text] | join("")), usage}'
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$headers = @{ 'api-key' = $env:AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY; 'anthropic-version' = '2023-06-01' }
$body = @{
  model      = 'support-chat'
  max_tokens = 1024
  messages   = @(@{ role = 'user'; content = 'In one sentence, what is an AI gateway?' })
} | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5
$r = Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post -Uri "$($env:AI_GATEWAY_URL.TrimEnd('/'))/default/models/anthropic/v1/messages" `
  -Headers $headers -ContentType 'application/json' -Body $body
[pscustomobject]@{ model = $r.model; text = (@($r.content) | Where-Object type -eq 'text' | ForEach-Object text) -join ''; usage = $r.usage }
```

The response uses Anthropic's own format, with `content` blocks, `stop_reason`, and `usage.input_tokens`. It
doesn't use OpenAI's `choices`. The `model` field names the backend model that answered, for example
`claude-haiku-5-5`. Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 think adaptively by default, so `content` can start
with a `thinking` block, and thinking counts toward `max_tokens`. Read the `text` blocks and leave headroom in
`max_tokens`.

> **Checkpoint**
> The call returns a Claude reply, and `model` is `claude-haiku-5-5`. Your app never sent an Anthropic
> key.

## Give one backend model two aliases

The batch team's nightly job shouldn't be able to use up the capacity that the support app needs. Point a second
alias, `batch-chat`, at the same fast model and give each alias its own per-caller token limit: 2,000 tokens per
minute for `batch-chat` and 20,000 for `support-chat`. Alias policies apply only to callers that use that name.
Policies on the backend model apply to every alias that targets it.

<!-- track: portal | Portal -->

### Add the batch-chat alias

Select **Models** › **Aliases** › **Add alias**. The **Create alias** wizard has four steps:

| Step | What to do |
|---|---|
| **Basics** | Set **Alias name** to `batch-chat` and **Description** to `Nightly batch summaries`. |
| **Select models** | Under **Available backend models**, select `claude-haiku-5-5` from the `Anthropic` provider. |
| **Priority and weights** | Keep the defaults, priority `0` and weight `1`. With one backend model, it gets all requests. |
| **Review** | Check the summary. |

Select **Create**. You can also start from **Models** › **Add** › **Alias for an existing model**.

### Limit each alias

Select **Policies** › **Add policy**. On the **Type** step, select **Token rate limit**, then **Next**. On the
**Scope** step, select **Individual assets**, select the `batch-chat` alias, then **Next**. On the
**Configure** step, set **Time period** to **Per minute**, **Allowed tokens** to `2000`, and **Counter
dimensions** to **Caller identity**. Select **Create**.

Repeat for the `support-chat` alias with `20000` **Allowed tokens**.

> **Checkpoint**
> **Policies** lists two **Token rate limit** policies, one scoped to `batch-chat` and one scoped to
> `support-chat`.

<!-- track: rest | REST API -->

### Put both aliases with their limits

The optional fourth argument adds a per-caller token limit to the alias. It's the same `tokenLimit` policy
object that models use.

```bash title="Bash"
./infra/alias.sh put batch-chat   "$PROVIDER" "$FAST_MODEL" 2000
./infra/alias.sh put support-chat "$PROVIDER" "$FAST_MODEL" 20000
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
./infra/alias.ps1 -ResourceGroup $RG -Gateway $GATEWAY put batch-chat   $PROVIDER $FAST_MODEL 2000
./infra/alias.ps1 -ResourceGroup $RG -Gateway $GATEWAY put support-chat $PROVIDER $FAST_MODEL 20000
```

The body now carries a policy:

```json
"policies": [ { "type": "tokenLimit", "count": 2000, "period": "minute", "counterKey": ["identity"] } ]
```

A `PUT` replaces the whole alias, including its policies. To change only the target, use `retarget` in the
next section.

> **Checkpoint**
> Each command prints the alias with `tokenLimit 2000/minute` or `tokenLimit 20000/minute`.

<!-- /tracks -->

## Retarget an alias without touching clients

The support team wants better answers. Point `support-chat` at the bigger model. The clients keep sending
`"model": "support-chat"`, and the alias keeps its 20,000-token limit.

<!-- track: portal | Portal -->

### Edit the alias

In **Models** › **Aliases**, open the `support-chat` alias and select **Edit**. **Edit alias** has the same
steps as **Create alias**. On **Select models**, clear `claude-haiku-5-5` and select `claude-sonnet-5-5` from
the `Anthropic` provider. Keep the defaults on **Priority and weights**, select **Next** until you reach
**Review**, then select **Save**. New requests use the selected backend model immediately.

![The Priority and weights step of the alias wizard, with a backend model at priority 0 and two at priority 1 split 75/25](../assets/screens/models-alias-routing.png "Edit alias changes the backend models behind the name. The alias name that clients send stays the same. With several backend models, Priority and weights decides which one serves each request, as in lab 22.")

### Check that the policy stayed

On the `support-chat` alias page, select the **Policies** tab.

> **Checkpoint**
> The alias page shows `claude-sonnet-5-5` on the **Backend models** tab, and the **Policies** tab still lists the
> 20,000-token **Token rate limit**.

<!-- track: rest | REST API -->

### Patch only the backend model

`retarget` sends a `PATCH` that contains only `backendModels`, so the alias name, description, and policies stay
as they are.

```bash title="Bash"
./infra/alias.sh retarget support-chat "$PROVIDER" "$SMART_MODEL"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
./infra/alias.ps1 -ResourceGroup $RG -Gateway $GATEWAY retarget support-chat $PROVIDER $SMART_MODEL
```

```text
PATCH .../workspaces/default/aliases/support-chat?api-version=2025-09-01-preview
{ "properties": { "backendModels": [ { "resourceId": ".../modelProviders/anthropic/models/claude-sonnet-5-5" } ] } }
```

> **Checkpoint**
> The output shows `support-chat` → `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` and still `tokenLimit 20000/minute`.

<!-- /tracks -->

> [!NOTE]
> Retarget only between backend models that support the same interface. An alias that clients call with the
> Anthropic Messages API must keep pointing to a model that supports Anthropic Messages.

## Verify

<!-- steps -->

### List the aliases

```bash title="Bash"
./infra/alias.sh list
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
./infra/alias.ps1 -ResourceGroup $RG -Gateway $GATEWAY list
```

Expected output (the order and your Foundry alias differ):

```text
ALIAS                        PROVIDER/BACKEND MODEL       ALIAS POLICIES
anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5  anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5  -
batch-chat                   anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5   tokenLimit 2000/minute
contoso-ai/gpt-6-luna        contoso-ai/gpt-6-luna        -
support-chat                 anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5  tokenLimit 20000/minute
```

Your Foundry and Anthropic models sit side by side behind one gateway. In the portal, **Models** shows the same
list.

### Call both aliases

The script sends a Messages request and prints the status, the backend model that answered, and the reply.

```bash title="Bash"
./infra/call-anthropic.sh support-chat
./infra/call-anthropic.sh batch-chat
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
./infra/call-anthropic.ps1 -Alias support-chat
./infra/call-anthropic.ps1 -Alias batch-chat
```

On GitHub, open [call-anthropic.sh](infra/call-anthropic.sh) or [call-anthropic.ps1](infra/call-anthropic.ps1).

Expected output (the replies differ):

```text
Alias:   support-chat
Status:  200
Model:   claude-sonnet-5-5
Reply:   An AI gateway is a control point between applications and AI models that ...
Alias:   batch-chat
Status:  200
Model:   claude-haiku-5-5
Reply:   An AI gateway sits between your apps and AI models to ...
```

> **Checkpoint**
> `support-chat` now answers with Sonnet and `batch-chat` with Haiku, and you didn't change the client request.

### Confirm the alias kept its policy

```bash title="Bash"
./infra/alias.sh show support-chat | jq '.properties.policies'
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
(./infra/alias.ps1 -ResourceGroup $RG -Gateway $GATEWAY show support-chat | ConvertFrom-Json).properties.policies
```

The output lists the `tokenLimit` policy with `"count": 20000` and `"counterKey": ["identity"]`. In the portal,
open `support-chat` and select **Policies**.

<!-- /steps -->

## Go further

- **Use the Anthropic SDK.** Point the SDK at the gateway's Anthropic base URL. The SDK appends `/v1/messages`
  itself and sends `anthropic-version` for you.

  ```python
  import os
  from anthropic import Anthropic  # pip install anthropic

  client = Anthropic(
      base_url=os.environ["AI_GATEWAY_URL"].rstrip("/") + "/default/models/anthropic",
      api_key="unused",  # required by the SDK; the gateway reads the api-key header
      default_headers={"api-key": os.environ["AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY"]},
  )
  message = client.messages.create(
      model="support-chat",
      max_tokens=1024,
      messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
  )
  print(message.model, "".join(block.text for block in message.content if block.type == "text"))
  ```

- **Move one alias between providers.** Add OpenAI as a second custom provider with the values from the
  provider table, and register `gpt-6-luna` with **OpenAI chat completions**. Create an alias such as
  `team-chat` on your Foundry `gpt-6-luna`, then retarget it to the OpenAI model. Both speak Chat Completions,
  so clients don't notice the switch.
- **Layer the limits.** Add a token limit to the `claude-haiku-5-5` backend model as in
  [Throttle tokens per caller with token limits](../06-token-limits/README.md). It applies to every alias that
  targets the model, on top of each alias's own limit.

## Clean up

Keep the gateway, the runtime key, and the Foundry model from lab 02. Later labs use them. Remove what you added
in this lab in this order: aliases, then backend models, then the provider.

In the portal, open each of the `support-chat`, `batch-chat`, and `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` aliases in
**Models** and delete them. Then delete the two Claude backend models and the `Anthropic` provider.

From a shell:

```bash title="Bash"
for ALIAS in support-chat batch-chat "$PROVIDER/$SMART_MODEL"; do ./infra/alias.sh delete "$ALIAS"; done
for MODEL in "$FAST_MODEL" "$SMART_MODEL"; do
  az rest --method delete --url "$WS/modelProviders/$PROVIDER/models/$MODEL?$API"
done
az rest --method delete --url "$WS/modelProviders/$PROVIDER?$API"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
foreach ($alias in 'support-chat', 'batch-chat', "$PROVIDER/$SMART_MODEL") {
  ./infra/alias.ps1 -ResourceGroup $RG -Gateway $GATEWAY delete $alias
}
foreach ($model in $FAST_MODEL, $SMART_MODEL) {
  az rest --method delete --url "$WS/modelProviders/$PROVIDER/models/$model`?$API"
}
az rest --method delete --url "$WS/modelProviders/$PROVIDER`?$API"
```

Deleting the provider removes the stored Anthropic key from the gateway. It doesn't revoke the key itself. If
you created the key only for this lab, delete it in the Claude Console.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| The wizard discovers no models, or times out | The base endpoint URL includes `/v1`, the header name is wrong, or the provider doesn't serve `/v1/models` | Use `https://api.anthropic.com` and `x-api-key`. If the provider can't list models, add them with **Individual model**. |
| `401` from the gateway | The `api-key` header is missing or holds the Anthropic key instead of a gateway runtime key | Send a runtime key from **Access** › **Keys** in the `api-key` header. |
| An authentication error from Anthropic in the response body | The stored provider key is wrong or expired, or **Include Bearer** is selected for Anthropic | Update the provider's API key and clear **Authentication scheme**. |
| `400` that mentions `anthropic-version` | The request doesn't send the `anthropic-version` header | Add `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01`. |
| `404` or a "model not found" error | The `model` value doesn't exactly match an alias, or you called the OpenAI route for an Anthropic model | Copy the alias from **Models**, and call `/default/models/anthropic/v1/messages`. |
| "Callable aliases must be unique" | Another alias in the gateway already uses that name | Pick a different alias, or retarget the existing one. |

  purchased capacity behind one alias.

# Route an alias across models by priority and weight

Your team wants to try `gpt-6.1-sol`, but every app already sends `"model": "chat"`, and nobody wants a big-bang
switch. In this lab you put the current model and the new one behind the same alias, send a fifth of the traffic
to the new model, count where the requests land, and then use priority to choose which model is preferred. The
apps never change the model name they send.

![Clients call one alias. The gateway prefers the backend models with the lowest priority number and splits their traffic by weight](../assets/diagrams/alias-routing.svg "Priority picks the tier. Weight splits the traffic inside it.")

<!-- widget: alias-routing {"alias":"chat"} -->

## Before you begin

- Complete [Publish a Foundry model and make your first call](../02-first-model-call/README.md). You need the
  gateway, a runtime API key, and the `gpt-6-luna` backend model. Lab 02 also gave the gateway the
  **Foundry User** role on your Foundry account, which covers the new deployment in this lab.
- Permission to change the gateway, for example **Contributor** on its resource group, and to create deployments
  in the Foundry account.
- The [Azure CLI](https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/install-azure-cli) 2.75 or later, signed in with
  `az login`. The Bash commands also use `jq`; the PowerShell commands need PowerShell 7 or later.
- Optional: [Publish models from any provider behind stable aliases](../03-multi-provider-aliases/README.md)
  explains aliases in more depth.

Set these variables once. Every track and the **Verify** section reuse them.

```bash title="Bash"
export RG="<resource-group>"
export GATEWAY="<gateway>"
export FOUNDRY_RG="<foundry-resource-group>"     # resource group of the Foundry account from lab 02
export FOUNDRY_ACCOUNT="<foundry-account-name>"
export PROVIDER="foundry-models"                 # the gateway provider that holds gpt-6-luna
export PRIMARY="gpt-6-luna"                      # the backend model that serves today's traffic
export CANDIDATE="gpt-6.1-sol"                   # the new model to try
export CANDIDATE_VERSION="2026-09-29"
export ALIAS="chat"                              # the name that clients send in "model"

export API="api-version=2025-09-01-preview"
export GATEWAY_ID="$(az resource show -g "$RG" -n "$GATEWAY" --resource-type Microsoft.ApiManagement/aigateways --query id -o tsv)"
export GW="https://management.azure.com$GATEWAY_ID"
export WS="$GW/workspaces/default"
export FOUNDRY_ID="$(az cognitiveservices account show -g "$FOUNDRY_RG" -n "$FOUNDRY_ACCOUNT" --query id -o tsv)"
export AI_GATEWAY_URL="https://$(az resource show --ids "$GATEWAY_ID" --query properties.frontend.defaultHostname -o tsv)"
# Paste the gateway runtime key from lab 02. Don't commit it or write it to a file.
read -rsp "AI Gateway API key: " AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY && export AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY && echo
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$RG                = "<resource-group>"
$GATEWAY           = "<gateway>"
$FOUNDRY_RG        = "<foundry-resource-group>"    # resource group of the Foundry account from lab 02
$FOUNDRY_ACCOUNT   = "<foundry-account-name>"
$PROVIDER          = "foundry-models"              # the gateway provider that holds gpt-6-luna
$PRIMARY           = "gpt-6-luna"                  # the backend model that serves today's traffic
$CANDIDATE         = "gpt-6.1-sol"                 # the new model to try
$CANDIDATE_VERSION = "2026-09-29"
$ALIAS             = "chat"                        # the name that clients send in "model"

$API        = "api-version=2025-09-01-preview"
$GATEWAY_ID = az resource show -g $RG -n $GATEWAY --resource-type Microsoft.ApiManagement/aigateways --query id -o tsv
$GW         = "https://management.azure.com$GATEWAY_ID"
$WS         = "$GW/workspaces/default"
$FOUNDRY_ID = az cognitiveservices account show -g $FOUNDRY_RG -n $FOUNDRY_ACCOUNT --query id -o tsv
$env:AI_GATEWAY_URL = "https://$(az resource show --ids $GATEWAY_ID --query properties.frontend.defaultHostname -o tsv)"
# Paste the gateway runtime key from lab 02. Don't commit it or write it to a file.
$env:AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY = Read-Host "AI Gateway API key" -MaskInput
```

The CLI and Bicep tracks of lab 02 name the provider `foundry-models`. A portal import names it after your
Foundry account. To check, list the providers and the models of each one:

```bash title="Bash"
for p in $(az rest --url "$WS/modelProviders?$API" --query "value[].name" -o tsv); do
  echo "$p: $(az rest --url "$WS/modelProviders/$p/models?$API" --query "join(', ', value[].name)" -o tsv)"
done
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
foreach ($p in az rest --url "$WS/modelProviders`?$API" --query "value[].name" -o tsv) {
  "${p}: $(az rest --url "$WS/modelProviders/$p/models`?$API" --query "join(', ', value[].name)" -o tsv)"
}
```

Deploy the candidate model in the same Foundry account as `gpt-6-luna`. Pick a region where the model is
available. Model inference is billed per use.

```bash title="Bash"
az cognitiveservices account deployment create -g "$FOUNDRY_RG" -n "$FOUNDRY_ACCOUNT" \
  --deployment-name "$CANDIDATE" --model-name "$CANDIDATE" --model-version "$CANDIDATE_VERSION" \
  --model-format OpenAI --sku-name GlobalStandard --sku-capacity 10 \
  --query "{name:name, state:properties.provisioningState}"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
az cognitiveservices account deployment create -g $FOUNDRY_RG -n $FOUNDRY_ACCOUNT `
  --deployment-name $CANDIDATE --model-name $CANDIDATE --model-version $CANDIDATE_VERSION `
  --model-format OpenAI --sku-name GlobalStandard --sku-capacity 10 `
  --query "{name:name, state:properties.provisioningState}"
```

## How it works

An alias holds a list of backend models. Each one has a priority and a weight:

| Setting | Values | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Priority** | Whole number from 0 to 100 | `0` | Lower numbers are preferred. Requests go to the backend models with the lowest priority number. |
| **Weight** | Whole number from 1 to 100 | `1` | Splits traffic among the backend models that share a priority, in proportion to their weights. |

A backend model's **Share within priority** is its weight divided by the sum of the weights at its priority.
Weights `80` and `20` give 80% and 20%; weights `3` and `1` give 75% and 25%. With one backend model, the alias
behaves like the single-target aliases of labs 02 and 03.

Pick the values from the job you need to do:

| Scenario | Priority | Weight |
|---|---|---|
| **Canary a new model version** | Same for both | Small share for the new version, for example `95` and `5`, then raise it |
| **A/B test two models** | Same for both | Equal, for example `50` and `50` |
| **Balance deployments** across regions or providers | Same for all | In proportion to each deployment's capacity, for example `3` and `1` |
| **Prefer purchased capacity** | Provisioned deployment `0`, pay-as-you-go `1` | Any |

A few rules keep every request answerable:

- Each backend model can appear only once in an alias.
- All backend models must support at least one interface in common, for example **OpenAI Chat Completions**.
  Mixing an Anthropic Messages model with an OpenAI model in one alias fails.
- The response tells you which backend served the request: the `model` field holds the backend's model name and
  version, for example `gpt-6.1-sol-2026-09-29`, and Foundry models also return an `x-ms-served-model` header.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Priority sets a preference, not a guaranteed failover. In our preview tests, when the preferred backend
> returned an error such as `429` or `404`, the gateway passed that error to the client instead of retrying a
> lower-priority backend. Test how your gateway behaves under throttling before you rely on priority for
> availability, and keep retries in your clients.

## Split traffic 80/20 between two models

Register the candidate model in the gateway, then create the `chat` alias with both models at priority `0` and
weights `80` and `20`.

<!-- track: portal | Portal -->

### Import the candidate model

1. Open the [AI Gateway portal](https://ai.gateway.azure.com) and select your gateway in the top bar.
2. Select **Models** › **Add** › **Models from Microsoft Foundry**.
3. Select the subscription and resource group of your Foundry account, then select the `gpt-6.1-sol`
   deployment. Keep **Managed identity** as the **Authentication method**.
4. Select **Add models**. If the wizard also creates an alias named after the model, keep it; this lab doesn't
   use it.

### Create the chat alias

1. Select **Models** › **Aliases** › **Add alias**.
2. On **Basics**, set **Alias name** to `chat` and **Description** to `Canary: 80/20 between the current and the
   new model`. Select **Next**.
3. On **Select models**, select `gpt-6-luna` and `gpt-6.1-sol` in **Available backend models**. Select **Next**.
4. On **Priority and weights**, keep **Priority** at `0` for both models. Set **Weight** to `80` for
   `gpt-6-luna` and `20` for `gpt-6.1-sol`. **Share within priority** shows `80%` and `20%`. Select **Next**.
5. On **Review**, check the shares, then select **Create**.

![The Priority and weights step of Create alias, with Priority, Weight, and Share within priority columns for each backend model](../assets/screens/models-alias-routing.png "Priority and weights. This example from the product documentation uses three GPT-4o deployments: one at priority 0, and two at priority 1 that split 75/25.")

> **Checkpoint**
> **Models** › **Aliases** lists `chat`. Its **Backend models** tab shows `gpt-6-luna` and `gpt-6.1-sol`, both at
> priority `0`, with weights `80` and `20`.

<!-- track: cli | Azure CLI -->

### Register the candidate model

A backend model registers one deployment under the provider. This is the same call as in lab 02, with the
model version.

```bash title="Bash"
az rest --method put --url "$WS/modelProviders/$PROVIDER/models/$CANDIDATE?$API" \
  --body "$(jq -cn --arg id "$FOUNDRY_ID/deployments/$CANDIDATE" --arg d "$CANDIDATE" --arg v "$CANDIDATE_VERSION" '{properties: {
      displayName: $d, apiFormat: "OpenAIChatCompletions",
      supportedEndpoints: ["/openai/v1/chat/completions", "/openai/v1/responses"],
      deployment: {resourceId: $id, modelName: $d, modelVersion: $v}}}')" \
  --query "{name:name, version:properties.deployment.modelVersion}"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
@{ properties = @{
    displayName        = $CANDIDATE
    apiFormat          = "OpenAIChatCompletions"
    supportedEndpoints = @("/openai/v1/chat/completions", "/openai/v1/responses")
    deployment         = @{ resourceId = "$FOUNDRY_ID/deployments/$CANDIDATE"; modelName = $CANDIDATE; modelVersion = $CANDIDATE_VERSION }
  } } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10 -Compress | Set-Content body.json
az rest --method put --url "$WS/modelProviders/$PROVIDER/models/$CANDIDATE`?$API" --body "@body.json" `
  --query "{name:name, version:properties.deployment.modelVersion}"
Remove-Item body.json
```

### Create the chat alias

Each entry in `backendModels` has a `resourceId`, a `priority`, and a `weight`.

```bash title="Bash"
export MODELS="$GATEWAY_ID/workspaces/default/modelProviders/$PROVIDER/models"
az rest --method put --url "$WS/aliases/$ALIAS?$API" \
  --body "$(jq -cn --arg p "$MODELS/$PRIMARY" --arg c "$MODELS/$CANDIDATE" '{properties: {
      description: "Canary: 80/20 between the current and the new model",
      backendModels: [
        {resourceId: $p, priority: 0, weight: 80},
        {resourceId: $c, priority: 0, weight: 20}]}}')" \
  --query properties.backendModels -o json |
  jq -r '.[] | "\(.resourceId | split("/") | last)  priority \(.priority)  weight \(.weight)"'
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$MODELS = "$GATEWAY_ID/workspaces/default/modelProviders/$PROVIDER/models"
@{ properties = @{
    description   = "Canary: 80/20 between the current and the new model"
    backendModels = @(
      @{ resourceId = "$MODELS/$PRIMARY";   priority = 0; weight = 80 }
      @{ resourceId = "$MODELS/$CANDIDATE"; priority = 0; weight = 20 }
    ) } } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10 -Compress | Set-Content body.json
az rest --method put --url "$WS/aliases/$ALIAS`?$API" --body "@body.json" --query properties.backendModels -o json |
  ConvertFrom-Json | ForEach-Object { '{0}  priority {1}  weight {2}' -f ($_.resourceId -split '/')[-1], $_.priority, $_.weight }
Remove-Item body.json
```

> **Checkpoint**
> The output shows `gpt-6-luna  priority 0  weight 80` and `gpt-6.1-sol  priority 0  weight 20`.

<!-- track: iac | Bicep -->

### Review the template

The template registers the candidate deployment under the existing provider and publishes the alias. It only
references `gpt-6-luna`, so the token limit that lab 02 put on that model stays. The `strategy` parameter
switches between a weighted split and a priority preference.

<!-- include: infra/main.bicep -->

On GitHub, open [infra/main.bicep](infra/main.bicep).

### Deploy the weighted split

```bash title="Bash"
az deployment group create -g "$RG" --template-file infra/main.bicep \
  --parameters gatewayName="$GATEWAY" providerName="$PROVIDER" primaryModelName="$PRIMARY" \
               foundryAccountId="$FOUNDRY_ID" candidateDeploymentName="$CANDIDATE" \
               candidateModelVersion="$CANDIDATE_VERSION" aliasName="$ALIAS" \
               strategy=weighted candidateWeight=20 \
  --query properties.outputs.routes.value
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
az deployment group create -g $RG --template-file infra/main.bicep `
  --parameters gatewayName=$GATEWAY providerName=$PROVIDER primaryModelName=$PRIMARY `
               foundryAccountId=$FOUNDRY_ID candidateDeploymentName=$CANDIDATE `
               candidateModelVersion=$CANDIDATE_VERSION aliasName=$ALIAS `
               strategy=weighted candidateWeight=20 `
  --query properties.outputs.routes.value
```

> **Checkpoint**
> The `routes` output lists `gpt-6-luna` with `priority 0` and `weight 80`, and `gpt-6.1-sol` with `priority 0`
> and `weight 20`.

<!-- /tracks -->

## Watch the split

Send 20 requests to `chat` and count which backend model answered each one. The script sends one request every
half second and reads the `model` field of each response.

```bash title="Bash"
./infra/count-models.sh "$ALIAS" 20
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
./infra/count-models.ps1 -Alias $ALIAS -Count 20
```

```text
Requests per backend model:
  16 gpt-6-luna-2026-09-22
   4 gpt-6.1-sol-2026-09-29
```

In our tests the gateway interleaved the two models, four requests to `gpt-6-luna` and then one to
`gpt-6.1-sol`, so 20 requests split exactly 16 and 4. Plan around the shares, not the exact order.

To see the header for a single call:

```bash title="Bash"
curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null "$AI_GATEWAY_URL/default/models/openai/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "api-key: $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"model\": \"$ALIAS\", \"max_completion_tokens\": 16, \"messages\": [{\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"Hi\"}]}" |
  grep -i "^x-ms-served-model"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$body = @{ model = $ALIAS; max_completion_tokens = 16; messages = @(@{ role = "user"; content = "Hi" }) } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress
(Invoke-WebRequest -Method Post -Uri "$env:AI_GATEWAY_URL/default/models/openai/v1/chat/completions" `
  -Headers @{ "api-key" = $env:AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY } -ContentType "application/json" -Body $body).Headers["x-ms-served-model"]
```

> **Checkpoint**
> About four of every five requests show `gpt-6-luna-…`, and the rest show `gpt-6.1-sol-…`. The client sent
> `"model": "chat"` every time.

## Prefer one model by priority

The canary looks good, but finance wants `gpt-6-luna` to handle the traffic until the new model is approved.
Give `gpt-6.1-sol` priority `1`. It stays in the alias, ready to promote, but requests go to `gpt-6-luna`.

<!-- track: portal | Portal -->

### Edit the alias

1. In **Models** › **Aliases**, open `chat` and select **Edit**.
2. Select **Next** until you reach **Priority and weights**.
3. Set **Priority** to `1` for `gpt-6.1-sol` and set both weights to `1`. `gpt-6-luna` now shows `100%` at
   priority `0`, and `gpt-6.1-sol` shows `100%` at priority `1`.
4. Select **Next**, then **Save**. New requests use the new settings immediately.

> **Checkpoint**
> The alias **Backend models** tab shows `gpt-6-luna` at priority `0` and `gpt-6.1-sol` at priority `1`.

<!-- track: cli | Azure CLI -->

### Put the new priorities

A `PUT` replaces the whole list, so send both backend models.

```bash title="Bash"
az rest --method put --url "$WS/aliases/$ALIAS?$API" \
  --body "$(jq -cn --arg p "$MODELS/$PRIMARY" --arg c "$MODELS/$CANDIDATE" '{properties: {
      description: "Prefer the current model",
      backendModels: [
        {resourceId: $p, priority: 0, weight: 1},
        {resourceId: $c, priority: 1, weight: 1}]}}')" \
  --query properties.backendModels -o json |
  jq -r '.[] | "\(.resourceId | split("/") | last)  priority \(.priority)  weight \(.weight)"'
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
@{ properties = @{
    description   = "Prefer the current model"
    backendModels = @(
      @{ resourceId = "$MODELS/$PRIMARY";   priority = 0; weight = 1 }
      @{ resourceId = "$MODELS/$CANDIDATE"; priority = 1; weight = 1 }
    ) } } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10 -Compress | Set-Content body.json
az rest --method put --url "$WS/aliases/$ALIAS`?$API" --body "@body.json" --query properties.backendModels -o json |
  ConvertFrom-Json | ForEach-Object { '{0}  priority {1}  weight {2}' -f ($_.resourceId -split '/')[-1], $_.priority, $_.weight }
Remove-Item body.json
```

> **Checkpoint**
> The output shows `gpt-6-luna  priority 0  weight 1` and `gpt-6.1-sol  priority 1  weight 1`.

<!-- track: iac | Bicep -->

### Deploy the priority strategy

Run the same template with `strategy=priority`.

```bash title="Bash"
az deployment group create -g "$RG" --template-file infra/main.bicep \
  --parameters gatewayName="$GATEWAY" providerName="$PROVIDER" primaryModelName="$PRIMARY" \
               foundryAccountId="$FOUNDRY_ID" candidateDeploymentName="$CANDIDATE" \
               candidateModelVersion="$CANDIDATE_VERSION" aliasName="$ALIAS" \
               strategy=priority \
  --query properties.outputs.routes.value
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
az deployment group create -g $RG --template-file infra/main.bicep `
  --parameters gatewayName=$GATEWAY providerName=$PROVIDER primaryModelName=$PRIMARY `
               foundryAccountId=$FOUNDRY_ID candidateDeploymentName=$CANDIDATE `
               candidateModelVersion=$CANDIDATE_VERSION aliasName=$ALIAS `
               strategy=priority `
  --query properties.outputs.routes.value
```

> **Checkpoint**
> The `routes` output lists `gpt-6-luna` with `priority 0` and `gpt-6.1-sol` with `priority 1`.
