# Call backends with managed identities

Your platform team runs one gateway per region, and every gateway calls the same Foundry account. Today each
gateway uses its own system-assigned identity, so every new gateway needs a fresh **Foundry User** grant, and
recreating a gateway leaves a stale role assignment behind. The team wants one identity that it owns, grants
once, and attaches to every gateway, with no backend key stored anywhere. In this lab you check the gateway's
system-assigned identity, create a user-assigned identity, give it access to Foundry, and switch a model
provider to it without changing a single client.

![Callers authenticate inbound to the gateway, and the gateway authenticates outbound to each backend](../assets/diagrams/identity-boundaries.svg "Callers authenticate to the gateway with an API key or a Microsoft Entra token. The gateway then calls each backend with its own managed identity, which this lab configures.")

## Before you begin

- Complete [Publish a Foundry model and make your first call](../02-first-model-call/README.md). You need a
  gateway with a Foundry model provider that uses a managed identity, a model alias, and a runtime API key.
- The [Azure CLI](https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/install-azure-cli) 2.75 or later, signed in with
  `az login`. Every track uses it at least once: the portal can't change the identity of a model provider that
  already exists. The commands call the Azure Resource Manager REST API with `az rest`, because the
  `az aigateway` extension doesn't manage the new `aigateways` resource type yet.
- For the Bash commands: [jq](https://jqlang.org/download/), which builds the request bodies.
- Permissions:
  - Create a managed identity in the resource group, for example **Contributor** or
    **Managed Identity Contributor**.
  - Attach the identity to the gateway: **Contributor** on the gateway and **Managed Identity Operator** on the
    identity. **Contributor** on a resource group that holds both covers this.
  - Create role assignments on the Foundry account, for example **Owner**, **User Access Administrator**, or
    **Role Based Access Control Administrator**.

Managed identities are free. Nothing in this lab adds charges beyond the model calls you make.

Set these variables once. Every track and the **Verify** section reuse them.

```bash title="Bash"
export RG="<resource-group>"
export GATEWAY="<gateway>"
export PROVIDER="<provider-name>"                 # the Foundry provider from lab 02, for example foundry-models
export FOUNDRY_RG="<foundry-resource-group>"      # resource group of the Foundry account
export FOUNDRY_ACCOUNT="<foundry-account-name>"   # the account name, not a project or deployment name
export IDENTITY="id-aigateway-backends"           # the user-assigned identity to create

export API="api-version=2025-09-01-preview"
export GATEWAY_ID="$(az resource show -g "$RG" -n "$GATEWAY" --resource-type Microsoft.ApiManagement/aigateways --query id -o tsv)"
export GW="https://management.azure.com$GATEWAY_ID"
export WS="$GW/workspaces/default"
export FOUNDRY_ID="$(az cognitiveservices account show -g "$FOUNDRY_RG" -n "$FOUNDRY_ACCOUNT" --query id -o tsv)"
export AI_GATEWAY_URL="https://$(az resource show --ids "$GATEWAY_ID" --query properties.frontend.defaultHostname -o tsv)"
export AI_GATEWAY_MODEL="<model-name>"            # the alias you called in lab 02
# Paste the runtime key from lab 02. Don't commit it or write it to a file.
read -rsp "AI Gateway API key: " AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY && export AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY && echo
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$RG              = "<resource-group>"
$GATEWAY         = "<gateway>"
$PROVIDER        = "<provider-name>"              # the Foundry provider from lab 02, for example foundry-models
$FOUNDRY_RG      = "<foundry-resource-group>"     # resource group of the Foundry account
$FOUNDRY_ACCOUNT = "<foundry-account-name>"       # the account name, not a project or deployment name
$IDENTITY        = "id-aigateway-backends"        # the user-assigned identity to create

$API        = "api-version=2025-09-01-preview"
$GATEWAY_ID = az resource show -g $RG -n $GATEWAY --resource-type Microsoft.ApiManagement/aigateways --query id -o tsv
$GW         = "https://management.azure.com$GATEWAY_ID"
$WS         = "$GW/workspaces/default"
$FOUNDRY_ID = az cognitiveservices account show -g $FOUNDRY_RG -n $FOUNDRY_ACCOUNT --query id -o tsv
$env:AI_GATEWAY_URL = "https://$(az resource show --ids $GATEWAY_ID --query properties.frontend.defaultHostname -o tsv)"
$env:AI_GATEWAY_MODEL = "<model-name>"            # the alias you called in lab 02
# Paste the runtime key from lab 02. Don't commit it or write it to a file.
$env:AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY = Read-Host "AI Gateway API key" -MaskInput
```

Don't remember the provider name? List the Foundry providers:
`az rest --url "$WS/modelProviders?$API" --query "value[?properties.kind=='Foundry'].name" -o tsv`.

## How it works

Every call crosses two boundaries. **Inbound**, the caller proves who it is to the gateway with a runtime API key
([lab 10](../10-api-keys/README.md)) or a Microsoft Entra token ([lab 11](../11-entra-rbac/README.md)).
**Outbound**, the gateway proves who *it* is to the backend. The caller never sends a backend credential: you
configure it once on the asset, such as a model provider or an MCP server backend.

For Azure backends, use a managed identity. The gateway requests a Microsoft Entra token for the backend's
audience, `https://cognitiveservices.azure.com/` for Foundry, and Azure RBAC on the backend decides what the
identity can do. For Foundry and Azure OpenAI, grant **Foundry User** on the account. Keep backend API keys for
backends that can't accept an Entra token.

| | System-assigned identity | User-assigned identity | Stored backend key |
|---|---|---|---|
| Created by | Azure, with the gateway. The portal enables it by default. | You, as its own Azure resource | The backend's owner |
| Lifecycle | Tied to the gateway. Deleting the gateway deletes it. | Independent. Attach it to many gateways and keep it when a gateway is recreated. | You store it in the gateway and rotate it |
| Best for | One gateway calling Azure backends | Sharing one identity and its role assignments across gateways | Third-party providers and tools without Entra support |
| Foundry provider setting | `managedIdentity` without `clientId` | `managedIdentity.clientId` set to the identity's client ID | `apiKey` |

Attaching an identity to the gateway doesn't change which identity an asset uses. Each asset names its identity,
so you can move assets one at a time.

## Check the system-assigned identity

Lab 02's provider calls Foundry with the gateway's system-assigned identity. See it before you change anything.

<!-- steps -->

### Look at the identity in the portal

1. Open the [AI Gateway portal](https://ai.gateway.azure.com) and select your gateway.
2. Select **Managed identities**. On **Configure identities**, the **System-assigned identity** card shows
   **Enabled** with a **Principal ID** and a **Tenant ID**.
3. Select **View access**. **Backend access** lists the assets that authenticate with a managed identity. Your
   Foundry provider appears with **System-assigned** as its identity and **Foundry User** as its role.

![The Managed identities page with the system-assigned identity enabled and no user-assigned identities](../assets/screens/managed-identities.png "Configure identities shows the system-assigned identity's principal and tenant IDs, and the user-assigned identities attached to the gateway.")

### Check it with the CLI

```bash title="Bash"
az rest --url "$GW?$API" --query identity -o json
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
az rest --url "$GW`?$API" --query identity -o json
```

The output shows `type`, which includes `SystemAssigned`, and the system-assigned `principalId` and `tenantId`.
If the output is empty or `type` is `None`, enable the identity, wait for the gateway to finish updating, and
grant the new principal **Foundry User** on the Foundry account:

```bash title="Bash"
az rest --method patch --url "$GW?$API" --body '{"identity":{"type":"SystemAssigned"}}' -o none
az resource wait --ids "$GATEWAY_ID" --api-version 2025-09-01-preview --custom "properties.provisioningState=='Succeeded'"
PRINCIPAL_ID="$(az resource show --ids "$GATEWAY_ID" --query identity.principalId -o tsv)"
az role assignment create --assignee-object-id "$PRINCIPAL_ID" --assignee-principal-type ServicePrincipal \
  --role "53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d" --scope "$FOUNDRY_ID"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
'{"identity":{"type":"SystemAssigned"}}' | Set-Content identity.json
az rest --method patch --url "$GW`?$API" --body "@identity.json" -o none
az resource wait --ids $GATEWAY_ID --api-version 2025-09-01-preview --custom "properties.provisioningState=='Succeeded'"
Remove-Item identity.json
$PRINCIPAL_ID = az resource show --ids $GATEWAY_ID --query identity.principalId -o tsv
az role assignment create --assignee-object-id $PRINCIPAL_ID --assignee-principal-type ServicePrincipal `
  --role "53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d" --scope $FOUNDRY_ID
```

<!-- /steps -->

> [!WARNING]
> Don't turn off the system-assigned identity while assets use it. Disabling it recycles the service principal:
> every backend configured with it fails until you enable it again, and a re-enabled identity gets a new
> principal ID without the old role assignments.

## Create a user-assigned identity and give it access

Pick one track. Each track creates the identity, attaches it to the gateway, and grants it **Foundry User** on
the Foundry account.

<!-- track: portal | Portal -->

### Create and attach the identity

1. In **Managed identities** › **Configure identities**, under **User-assigned identities**, select
   **Add identity**.
2. Select **Create new** and enter the **Name** from `$IDENTITY`, for example `id-aigateway-backends`. The portal
   creates the identity in the gateway's subscription, resource group, and region.
3. Select **Add identity**. The new identity appears in the table with its **Principal** and **Client ID**.

To reuse an identity that already exists, select **Use existing** instead, then pick its **Subscription** and
**User-assigned managed identity**.

### Read the identity's IDs

You need the principal ID to grant access and the client ID to point the provider at the identity.

```bash title="Bash"
export IDENTITY_ID="$(az identity show -g "$RG" -n "$IDENTITY" --query id -o tsv)"
export IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID="$(az identity show -g "$RG" -n "$IDENTITY" --query clientId -o tsv)"
export IDENTITY_PRINCIPAL_ID="$(az identity show -g "$RG" -n "$IDENTITY" --query principalId -o tsv)"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$IDENTITY_ID           = az identity show -g $RG -n $IDENTITY --query id -o tsv
$IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID    = az identity show -g $RG -n $IDENTITY --query clientId -o tsv
$IDENTITY_PRINCIPAL_ID = az identity show -g $RG -n $IDENTITY --query principalId -o tsv
```

### Grant Foundry User on the Foundry account

Attaching an identity doesn't grant it any access. In the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com), open the
Foundry account and select **Access control (IAM)** › **Add** › **Add role assignment**. Select **Foundry User**,
assign access to **Managed identity**, select your identity as the member, then select **Review + assign**.

Or grant the role from the command line:

```bash title="Bash"
az role assignment create --assignee-object-id "$IDENTITY_PRINCIPAL_ID" --assignee-principal-type ServicePrincipal \
  --role "53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d" --scope "$FOUNDRY_ID"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
az role assignment create --assignee-object-id $IDENTITY_PRINCIPAL_ID --assignee-principal-type ServicePrincipal `
  --role "53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d" --scope $FOUNDRY_ID
```

> **Checkpoint**
> **User-assigned identities** lists your identity, and the Foundry account's **Access control (IAM)** ›
> **Role assignments** shows it with **Foundry User**.

<!-- track: cli | Azure CLI -->

### Create the identity

```bash title="Bash"
az identity create -g "$RG" -n "$IDENTITY"

export IDENTITY_ID="$(az identity show -g "$RG" -n "$IDENTITY" --query id -o tsv)"
export IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID="$(az identity show -g "$RG" -n "$IDENTITY" --query clientId -o tsv)"
export IDENTITY_PRINCIPAL_ID="$(az identity show -g "$RG" -n "$IDENTITY" --query principalId -o tsv)"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
az identity create -g $RG -n $IDENTITY

$IDENTITY_ID           = az identity show -g $RG -n $IDENTITY --query id -o tsv
$IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID    = az identity show -g $RG -n $IDENTITY --query clientId -o tsv
$IDENTITY_PRINCIPAL_ID = az identity show -g $RG -n $IDENTITY --query principalId -o tsv
```

The identity is created in the resource group's region. It can live in any resource group or subscription in
the gateway's tenant.

### Attach it to the gateway

The request lists both identity types, so the system-assigned identity stays enabled. Changing the gateway's
identity runs in the background; `az resource wait` returns when the gateway is ready again.

```bash title="Bash"
jq -cn --arg id "$IDENTITY_ID" \
  '{identity:{type:"SystemAssigned, UserAssigned",userAssignedIdentities:{($id):{}}}}' > identity.json
az rest --method patch --url "$GW?$API" --body @identity.json -o none
az resource wait --ids "$GATEWAY_ID" --api-version 2025-09-01-preview --custom "properties.provisioningState=='Succeeded'"
rm identity.json
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
@{ identity = @{ type = "SystemAssigned, UserAssigned"; userAssignedIdentities = @{ $IDENTITY_ID = @{} } } } |
  ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10 -Compress | Set-Content identity.json
az rest --method patch --url "$GW`?$API" --body "@identity.json" -o none
az resource wait --ids $GATEWAY_ID --api-version 2025-09-01-preview --custom "properties.provisioningState=='Succeeded'"
Remove-Item identity.json
```

### Grant Foundry User on the Foundry account

```bash title="Bash"
az role assignment create --assignee-object-id "$IDENTITY_PRINCIPAL_ID" --assignee-principal-type ServicePrincipal \
  --role "53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d" --scope "$FOUNDRY_ID"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
az role assignment create --assignee-object-id $IDENTITY_PRINCIPAL_ID --assignee-principal-type ServicePrincipal `
  --role "53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d" --scope $FOUNDRY_ID
```

Grant the role on the Foundry account itself, the resource that the provider calls.

> **Checkpoint**
> `az rest --url "$GW?$API" --query identity.userAssignedIdentities -o json` lists your identity, with its
> `clientId` and `principalId`, and
> `az role assignment list --assignee "$IDENTITY_PRINCIPAL_ID" --scope "$FOUNDRY_ID" --query "[].roleDefinitionName" -o tsv`
> prints `Foundry User`.

<!-- track: iac | Bicep -->

### Review the template

[infra/main.bicep](infra/main.bicep) creates the user-assigned identity and calls
[infra/foundry-user-role.bicep](infra/foundry-user-role.bicep) in the Foundry account's resource group to grant
it **Foundry User**. The account can be in another resource group or subscription.

<!-- include: infra/main.bicep -->

<!-- include: infra/foundry-user-role.bicep -->

### Deploy the template

```bash title="Bash"
az deployment group create -g "$RG" \
  --template-file infra/main.bicep \
  --parameters identityName="$IDENTITY" foundryAccountId="$FOUNDRY_ID" \
  --query properties.outputs -o json

export IDENTITY_ID="$(az identity show -g "$RG" -n "$IDENTITY" --query id -o tsv)"
export IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID="$(az identity show -g "$RG" -n "$IDENTITY" --query clientId -o tsv)"
export IDENTITY_PRINCIPAL_ID="$(az identity show -g "$RG" -n "$IDENTITY" --query principalId -o tsv)"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
az deployment group create -g $RG `
  --template-file infra/main.bicep `
  --parameters identityName=$IDENTITY foundryAccountId=$FOUNDRY_ID `
  --query properties.outputs -o json

$IDENTITY_ID           = az identity show -g $RG -n $IDENTITY --query id -o tsv
$IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID    = az identity show -g $RG -n $IDENTITY --query clientId -o tsv
$IDENTITY_PRINCIPAL_ID = az identity show -g $RG -n $IDENTITY --query principalId -o tsv
```

The outputs show `identityId`, `clientId`, `principalId`, and the role assignment name.

### Attach the identity to the gateway

The template doesn't declare the gateway: an identity block in Bicep redeploys the whole gateway resource. Attach
the identity with the CLI instead. The request lists both identity types, so the system-assigned identity stays
enabled.

```bash title="Bash"
jq -cn --arg id "$IDENTITY_ID" \
  '{identity:{type:"SystemAssigned, UserAssigned",userAssignedIdentities:{($id):{}}}}' > identity.json
az rest --method patch --url "$GW?$API" --body @identity.json -o none
az resource wait --ids "$GATEWAY_ID" --api-version 2025-09-01-preview --custom "properties.provisioningState=='Succeeded'"
rm identity.json
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
@{ identity = @{ type = "SystemAssigned, UserAssigned"; userAssignedIdentities = @{ $IDENTITY_ID = @{} } } } |
  ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10 -Compress | Set-Content identity.json
az rest --method patch --url "$GW`?$API" --body "@identity.json" -o none
az resource wait --ids $GATEWAY_ID --api-version 2025-09-01-preview --custom "properties.provisioningState=='Succeeded'"
Remove-Item identity.json
```

> **Checkpoint**
> The deployment succeeds, and `az rest --url "$GW?$API" --query identity.userAssignedIdentities -o json` lists
> your identity.

<!-- /tracks -->

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Role assignments can take several minutes to take effect. If you switch the provider before then, model calls
> fail with `403` from the backend until the assignment propagates.

## Point the model provider at the identity

The provider still uses the system-assigned identity. Setting `clientId` in its managed identity settings
switches it to your identity. Clients don't change: they keep calling the same alias with the same key or token.

<!-- track: portal | Portal -->

### Update the provider's authentication

The portal picks the identity only when you import a Foundry account: the **Authentication method** step offers
**Managed identity** with a choice of the system-assigned identity or any attached user-assigned identity, and
grants the selected identity **Foundry User**. To switch a provider that already exists, run these Azure CLI
commands, for example in [Azure Cloud Shell](https://shell.azure.com). They read the provider's `foundry`
settings, set `clientId`, and write the settings back:

```bash title="Bash"
az rest --url "$WS/modelProviders/$PROVIDER?$API" --query properties.foundry -o json \
  | jq -c --arg c "$IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID" '{properties:{foundry:(.authentication.managedIdentity.clientId=$c)}}' \
  > provider.json
az rest --method patch --url "$WS/modelProviders/$PROVIDER?$API" --body @provider.json \
  --query properties.foundry.authentication
rm provider.json
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$foundry = az rest --url "$WS/modelProviders/${PROVIDER}?$API" --query properties.foundry -o json | ConvertFrom-Json
$foundry.authentication.managedIdentity |
  Add-Member -NotePropertyName clientId -NotePropertyValue $IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID -Force
@{ properties = @{ foundry = $foundry } } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10 -Compress | Set-Content provider.json
az rest --method patch --url "$WS/modelProviders/${PROVIDER}?$API" --body "@provider.json" `
  --query properties.foundry.authentication
Remove-Item provider.json
```

<!-- track: cli | Azure CLI -->

### Update the provider's authentication

A `PATCH` of `properties.foundry` replaces the whole `foundry` object, so a body with only `authentication`
fails. Read the current settings, set `clientId`, and send the whole object back. The endpoint and accounts stay
as they are, and models are separate resources.

```bash title="Bash"
az rest --url "$WS/modelProviders/$PROVIDER?$API" --query properties.foundry -o json \
  | jq -c --arg c "$IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID" '{properties:{foundry:(.authentication.managedIdentity.clientId=$c)}}' \
  > provider.json
az rest --method patch --url "$WS/modelProviders/$PROVIDER?$API" --body @provider.json \
  --query properties.foundry.authentication
rm provider.json
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$foundry = az rest --url "$WS/modelProviders/${PROVIDER}?$API" --query properties.foundry -o json | ConvertFrom-Json
$foundry.authentication.managedIdentity |
  Add-Member -NotePropertyName clientId -NotePropertyValue $IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID -Force
@{ properties = @{ foundry = $foundry } } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10 -Compress | Set-Content provider.json
az rest --method patch --url "$WS/modelProviders/${PROVIDER}?$API" --body "@provider.json" `
  --query properties.foundry.authentication
Remove-Item provider.json
```

<!-- track: iac | Bicep -->

### Redeploy the provider with the identity

[infra/provider.bicep](infra/provider.bicep) redeploys the provider that lab 02's Bicep track creates, with the
same endpoint and account, and adds `clientId` to its managed identity settings. A deployment replaces the
provider's properties, so pass the display name and description you want to keep. Models and aliases are
separate resources and aren't touched. If you created the provider in the portal or with
the CLI, use the **Azure CLI** track's commands instead, which change only the authentication.

```bicep
authentication: {
  kind: 'ManagedIdentity'
  managedIdentity: {
    clientId: identityClientId   // omit clientId to use the system-assigned identity
    resource: 'https://cognitiveservices.azure.com/'
  }
}
```

<!-- include: infra/provider.bicep -->

```bash title="Bash"
az deployment group create -g "$RG" \
  --template-file infra/provider.bicep \
  --parameters gatewayName="$GATEWAY" providerName="$PROVIDER" foundryAccountId="$FOUNDRY_ID" \
               identityClientId="$IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID" \
  --query properties.outputs -o json
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
az deployment group create -g $RG `
  --template-file infra/provider.bicep `
  --parameters gatewayName=$GATEWAY providerName=$PROVIDER foundryAccountId=$FOUNDRY_ID `
               identityClientId=$IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID `
  --query properties.outputs -o json
```

<!-- /tracks -->

> **Checkpoint**
> The provider's `authentication` shows `kind: ManagedIdentity` and a `managedIdentity.clientId` equal to
> `$IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID`.

## Verify

<!-- steps -->

### Confirm which identity the provider uses

```bash title="Bash"
az rest --url "$WS/modelProviders/$PROVIDER?$API" \
  --query properties.foundry.authentication.managedIdentity.clientId -o tsv
echo "$IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
az rest --url "$WS/modelProviders/${PROVIDER}?$API" `
  --query properties.foundry.authentication.managedIdentity.clientId -o tsv
$IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID
```

Both lines print the same client ID. In the portal, **Managed identities** › **View access** now lists your
provider under your identity's name instead of **System-assigned**. The list reflects the configured binding,
not the live role assignment on the Foundry account, so a missing role still shows up only as a failed call.

### Call the model through the gateway

```bash title="Bash"
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" "${AI_GATEWAY_URL%/}/default/models/openai/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "api-key: $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"model\":\"$AI_GATEWAY_MODEL\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"ping\"}]}"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$body = @{ model = $env:AI_GATEWAY_MODEL; messages = @(@{ role = "user"; content = "ping" }) } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5
(Invoke-WebRequest -Method Post -Uri "$($env:AI_GATEWAY_URL.TrimEnd('/'))/default/models/openai/v1/chat/completions" `
  -Headers @{ "api-key" = $env:AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY } -ContentType "application/json" -Body $body -SkipHttpErrorCheck).StatusCode
```

Expect `HTTP 200`. A `403` that mentions permissions on the Foundry account means the role assignment hasn't
propagated yet: wait a few minutes and retry.

You called the same alias with the same key as in lab 02. Only the gateway's outbound credential changed, and no
backend key was stored or sent.

<!-- /steps -->

> **Checkpoint**
> The provider names your user-assigned identity, **View access** shows the new binding, and the model still
> answers with `200`.

## Go further

### Use stored credentials when a backend can't take a managed identity

Managed identity needs a backend that accepts Microsoft Entra tokens. When it doesn't, store the backend's own
credential in the gateway, never in the calling app.

| Backend | How the gateway authenticates |
|---|---|
| Microsoft Foundry and Azure OpenAI | **Managed identity** (recommended) or **API key**, chosen in the import's **Authentication method** step |
| OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and other custom models | The provider's API key, entered when you add the custom model ([lab 03](../03-multi-provider-aliases/README.md)) |
| MCP server backends | **None**, **API key**, **OAuth 2.0**, or **Managed identity**, set per backend ([lab 04](../04-federate-mcp-tools/README.md)) |

- Prefer managed identity whenever the backend supports it.
- The gateway stores backend keys and tokens with the asset or connection and never returns them to clients.
- Rotate backend credentials on their own schedule. They're independent of the runtime keys callers use.

### Drop access the system identity no longer needs

After every asset that calls the Foundry account uses the user-assigned identity, the system-assigned identity's
**Foundry User** assignment on that account is unused. Check **View access** › **Backend access** first: remove
the assignment only if no other asset lists **System-assigned** for that account, because later labs in this
series use it. A call that still returns `200` a few minutes after you remove it also proves that the provider
uses the user-assigned identity.

## Clean up

Keep the system-assigned identity and its **Foundry User** role. Later labs use them. Remove the user-assigned
identity in this order, so the provider never points at an identity it can't use.

<!-- steps -->

### Switch the provider back to the system-assigned identity

Removing `clientId` selects the system-assigned identity again. As before, read the `foundry` settings, change
them, and write them back:

```bash title="Bash"
az rest --url "$WS/modelProviders/$PROVIDER?$API" --query properties.foundry -o json \
  | jq -c '{properties:{foundry:(del(.authentication.managedIdentity.clientId))}}' > provider.json
az rest --method patch --url "$WS/modelProviders/$PROVIDER?$API" --body @provider.json \
  --query properties.foundry.authentication
rm provider.json
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$foundry = az rest --url "$WS/modelProviders/${PROVIDER}?$API" --query properties.foundry -o json | ConvertFrom-Json
$foundry.authentication.managedIdentity.PSObject.Properties.Remove('clientId')
@{ properties = @{ foundry = $foundry } } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10 -Compress | Set-Content provider.json
az rest --method patch --url "$WS/modelProviders/${PROVIDER}?$API" --body "@provider.json" `
  --query properties.foundry.authentication
Remove-Item provider.json
```

The output no longer shows `clientId`.

If you used the Bicep track, redeploy `infra/provider.bicep` without `identityClientId` instead.

### Detach the identity from the gateway

Set the gateway's identity back to the system-assigned identity only:

```bash title="Bash"
az rest --method patch --url "$GW?$API" --body '{"identity":{"type":"SystemAssigned"}}' -o none
az resource wait --ids "$GATEWAY_ID" --api-version 2025-09-01-preview --custom "properties.provisioningState=='Succeeded'"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
'{"identity":{"type":"SystemAssigned"}}' | Set-Content identity.json
az rest --method patch --url "$GW`?$API" --body "@identity.json" -o none
az resource wait --ids $GATEWAY_ID --api-version 2025-09-01-preview --custom "properties.provisioningState=='Succeeded'"
Remove-Item identity.json
```

This detaches every user-assigned identity from the gateway and keeps the system-assigned one. If other assets
use another user-assigned identity on this gateway, detach yours in the portal instead.

In the portal, select the identity in **User-assigned identities**, select the delete button in the toolbar, then
**Detach**. Detaching removes the identity from this gateway only.

### Remove the role assignment and delete the identity

```bash title="Bash"
az role assignment delete --assignee "$IDENTITY_PRINCIPAL_ID" --role "53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d" --scope "$FOUNDRY_ID"
az identity delete -g "$RG" -n "$IDENTITY"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
az role assignment delete --assignee $IDENTITY_PRINCIPAL_ID --role "53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d" --scope $FOUNDRY_ID
az identity delete -g $RG -n $IDENTITY
```

Delete the role assignment first. Deleting the identity alone leaves an orphaned assignment on the account.

<!-- /steps -->

> **Checkpoint**
> The model call from **Verify** still returns `200`, and **View access** shows the provider under
> **System-assigned** again.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `403` mentioning permissions on the Foundry account right after the switch | The role assignment hasn't propagated, or it's at a different scope than the Foundry account | Wait a few minutes. Check `az role assignment list --assignee "$IDENTITY_PRINCIPAL_ID" --scope "$FOUNDRY_ID" -o table`. |
| Calls fail after the switch and the role is in place | `clientId` holds the principal (object) ID, or the identity isn't attached to the gateway | Use the identity's **Client ID**, and check that `az rest --url "$GW?$API" --query identity.userAssignedIdentities` lists the identity. |
| The `PATCH` that attaches the identity fails with an authorization error | You can't assign that identity to resources | Ask for **Managed Identity Operator** on the identity. |
| `az rest --url "$GW?$API" --query identity` prints nothing, or `type` is `None` | The gateway has no managed identity | Enable it with the `PATCH` in [Check the system-assigned identity](#check-the-system-assigned-identity), then grant it **Foundry User**. |
| Calls fail after you detach an identity or disable the system identity | An asset still uses that identity | Check **View access** › **Backend access** before you remove an identity, and switch those assets first. |
| `AuthorizationFailed` on `roleAssignments` | You can't create role assignments on the Foundry account | Ask for **Role Based Access Control Administrator** on the account, or have an owner grant the role. |

## Next steps

- [Go keyless with Microsoft Entra ID and RBAC](../11-entra-rbac/README.md): remove keys on the inbound side too.
- [Federate MCP tools behind one endpoint](../04-federate-mcp-tools/README.md): set backend authentication for tool servers.
- [Lock down backend traffic with private networking](../18-private-networking/README.md): keep backend traffic off the public internet.
- Docs: [Security and identity](https://ai.gateway.azure.com/docs/security-identity) and
  [Microsoft Foundry and AI Gateway](https://ai.gateway.azure.com/docs/foundry).

# Monitor usage, cost, and traces

Your gateway now serves several apps. Finance asks what the models cost per team, an app owner reports
intermittent failures, and nobody can tell whether a policy or the backend rejected those calls. In this lab you
send the gateway's OpenTelemetry signals to Application Insights and answer all three questions from the built-in
**Monitoring** dashboard, down to a single request's trace.

![AI Gateway exports metrics, logs, and traces to Application Insights or any OTLP endpoint](../assets/diagrams/observability.svg "The gateway exports each telemetry signal over OTLP. With Application Insights, the Monitoring page reads the same data back as a dashboard.")

<!-- widget: request-lifecycle -->

## Before you begin

- Complete [Publish a Foundry model and make your first call](../02-first-model-call/README.md). You need a gateway,
  an imported model, a callable alias, and a runtime API key from **Access** › **Keys**.
- Permission to change the gateway, for example **Contributor** on its resource group, **and** permission to
  create role assignments, for example **Owner** or **Role Based Access Control Administrator**. Setup grants the
  gateway's managed identity a role on the telemetry destination. To reuse an existing Application Insights
  resource, you also need **Application Insights Contributor** on it.
- To generate traffic: `curl` (Bash) or PowerShell 7. For the variable block below and the IaC track: the
  [Azure CLI](https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/install-azure-cli) 2.75 or later, signed in with `az login`.
  The commands read the gateway with `az resource` and `az rest`, because the `az aigateway` extension doesn't
  manage the new `aigateways` resource type yet.

Set these variables once. The tracks and the traffic script reuse them.

```bash title="Bash"
export RG="<resource-group>"
export GATEWAY="<gateway>"
export AI_GATEWAY_MODEL="<model-name>"     # a callable alias, for example the one you used in lab 02

export API="api-version=2025-09-01-preview"
export GATEWAY_ID="$(az resource show -g "$RG" -n "$GATEWAY" --resource-type Microsoft.ApiManagement/aigateways --query id -o tsv)"
export WS="https://management.azure.com$GATEWAY_ID/workspaces/default"
export AI_GATEWAY_URL="https://$(az resource show --ids "$GATEWAY_ID" --query properties.frontend.defaultHostname -o tsv)"
# Paste the runtime key you created in Access › Keys. Don't commit it or write it to a file.
read -rsp "AI Gateway API key: " AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY && export AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY && echo
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$RG      = "<resource-group>"
$GATEWAY = "<gateway>"
$env:AI_GATEWAY_MODEL = "<model-name>"     # a callable alias, for example the one you used in lab 02

$API        = "api-version=2025-09-01-preview"
$GATEWAY_ID = az resource show -g $RG -n $GATEWAY --resource-type Microsoft.ApiManagement/aigateways --query id -o tsv
$WS         = "https://management.azure.com$GATEWAY_ID/workspaces/default"
$env:AI_GATEWAY_URL = "https://$(az resource show --ids $GATEWAY_ID --query properties.frontend.defaultHostname -o tsv)"
# Paste the runtime key you created in Access › Keys. Don't commit it or write it to a file.
$env:AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY = Read-Host "AI Gateway API key" -MaskInput
```

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Did you configure monitoring before the 2026-08-28 release? Reconfigure it to get logs, traces, cost metrics, and
> policy spans: on the **Monitoring** page select **Settings**, disable monitoring, and configure it again. You can
> select the same Application Insights resource.

## How it works

The gateway emits three OpenTelemetry signals and exports each one **independently** over OTLP, to Azure Application
Insights or to any OTLP endpoint (for example Datadog, Splunk, Grafana Cloud, or your own collector). Configure only
the signals you need. Telemetry follows the OpenTelemetry GenAI and MCP semantic conventions, such as
`gen_ai.request.model`, `gen_ai.operation.name`, and `mcp.method.name`, and adds gateway attributes such as the API
key, alias, resolved model, and policy type.

When the destination is Application Insights and all three signals are on, the **Monitoring** page turns that data
into a dashboard. Estimated cost is **observed tokens × public pricing**: use it to spot trends and compare callers,
then reconcile with provider billing or Azure Cost Management for financial reporting.

| Signal | What the gateway sends | Where it lands with Application Insights | Dashboard uses it for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Metrics | Token usage and estimated token cost, by model, token type, API key, and caller | Azure Monitor workspace (managed Prometheus) linked to Application Insights | Tokens and **Estimated model cost** |
| Traces | One root span per request, with child spans for each stage and each policy that ran | `OTelSpans` table in the Log Analytics workspace | Calls, outcomes, blocked traces, the trace waterfall |
| Logs | Request records with status, caller, model, and the token usage the backend reported | `OTelLogs` table in the Log Analytics workspace | Correlated logs and caller attribution |

## Connect Application Insights

Pick one track. Both end with the gateway exporting all three signals to an Application Insights resource named
`<gateway>-insights`.

<!-- track: portal | Portal -->

### Start the setup

Open the [AI Gateway portal](https://ai.gateway.azure.com) and select your gateway from the gateway switcher. Select
**Monitoring**. If monitoring isn't configured yet, the page shows **Set up monitoring**. Select
**Configure telemetry**. The wizard has three steps: **Destination**, **Authentication**, and **Review and apply**.

### Choose a destination

On **Destination**, select **New Azure Application Insights resource** and keep the suggested name,
`<gateway>-insights`. Select **Next**.

> [!TIP]
> The other choices are **Existing Azure Application Insights resource** (the IaC track uses it) and
> **Custom OpenTelemetry destination**, which takes separate **Metrics endpoint**, **Logs endpoint**, and
> **Traces endpoint** URLs. Leave an endpoint empty to turn that signal off. The built-in dashboard only reads
> Application Insights, so with a custom destination you use your own platform's views.

### Review authentication

On **Authentication**, the gateway exports with its managed identity. If none is enabled, the wizard enables the
system-assigned identity for you. It also assigns the **Monitoring Metrics Publisher** role on the destination's
Data Collection Rule when you apply.

Leave **Include recommended token claims in telemetry** selected. It adds Microsoft Entra caller claims to the
telemetry, which [Attribute tokens and cost with OpenTelemetry](../14-otel-chargeback/README.md) builds on. Select
**Next**.

### Apply the configuration

On **Review and apply**, select **Apply**. The wizard shows each step as it runs: **Register resource providers**,
**Resolve managed identity**, **Provision destination**, **Discover OTLP endpoints**,
**Assign Monitoring Metrics Publisher role**, and **Create telemetry exporter**. If a step fails, fix the cause
shown in the message and select **Retry**. If an Azure Policy assignment blocks a step, check the Activity Log for
the denied operation.

> **Checkpoint**
> The **Monitoring** page shows the **Overview**, **Models**, **Tools**, **Policies**, and **Traces** tabs, with
> **Open in Azure portal** and **Settings** in the header.

<!-- track: iac | Bicep -->

### Choose what to declare

A complete monitoring setup declares three resources: a Log Analytics workspace, a workspace-based Application
Insights component, and a gateway telemetry exporter of kind `applicationInsights`. The current portal treats that exporter kind as
**legacy**: it no longer activates the OTLP signals the dashboard needs. The OpenTelemetry exporter that replaces it
depends on OTLP endpoints and a role assignment that Azure creates on the fly, and that wiring isn't documented for
automation yet.

So this template declares the destination exactly as the sample does, and you connect it in the portal in one step.
The sample's exporter block is in the file for reference, switched off by `deployLegacyExporter`.

### Review the template

<!-- include: infra/main.bicep -->

On GitHub, open [infra/main.bicep](infra/main.bicep).

### Deploy it

```bash title="Bash"
az deployment group create -g "$RG" \
  --template-file infra/main.bicep \
  --parameters gatewayName="$GATEWAY" \
  --query properties.outputs
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
az deployment group create -g $RG `
  --template-file infra/main.bicep `
  --parameters gatewayName=$GATEWAY `
  --query properties.outputs
```

The outputs list `appInsightsName` (`<gateway>-insights`) and the Log Analytics workspace ID.

### Connect the gateway to it

In the [AI Gateway portal](https://ai.gateway.azure.com), select your gateway, then **Monitoring** ›
**Configure telemetry**. On **Destination**, select **Existing Azure Application Insights resource**, and pick
`<gateway>-insights` in **Application Insights resource**. The wizard checks OTLP support and tells you it will be
enabled automatically when you apply. Select **Next**.

On **Authentication**, leave **Include recommended token claims in telemetry** selected and select **Next**. On
**Review and apply**, select **Apply** and wait for every step, ending with **Create telemetry exporter**.

> **Checkpoint**
> The **Monitoring** page shows the **Overview**, **Models**, **Tools**, **Policies**, and **Traces** tabs. In
> **Settings**, the destination is your `<gateway>-insights` resource and no legacy exporter warning is shown.

<!-- /tracks -->

## Generate traffic

The dashboard needs data. Send a few requests through the gateway so every view has something to show.

<!-- steps -->

### Run the traffic script

From the lab folder, run the script for your shell. It sends ten chat completions with an `x-correlation-id` header
on each, then one request for an alias that doesn't exist, so you also get a failure to investigate.

```bash title="Bash"
./infra/generate-traffic.sh "$AI_GATEWAY_MODEL" 10
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
./infra/generate-traffic.ps1 -Model $env:AI_GATEWAY_MODEL -Requests 10
```

On GitHub, open [generate-traffic.sh](infra/generate-traffic.sh) or
[generate-traffic.ps1](infra/generate-traffic.ps1).

Expected output: ten `200` rows and a final `error` row with a `4xx` status. Telemetry can take a few minutes to
reach the dashboard.

> [!TIP]
> Sending `x-correlation-id` from your apps makes application-level investigations easier. Never put personal data,
> secrets, prompts, or regulated identifiers in it.

<!-- /steps -->

## Tour the dashboard

Each tab answers a different question. Use the time range buttons (**1H**, **24H**, **7D**, **30D**) to match your
traffic.

<!-- steps -->

### Overview: is the gateway healthy, and what does it cost?

Select **Monitoring** › **Overview**. The cards summarize the range: **Estimated model cost**, **Model calls**,
**Tool calls**, **Trace failure rate**, and **Blocked traces**. Below them, **Model and tool calls over time**
stacks both kinds of traffic, **Top models** ranks models by estimated cost with their 4xx and 5xx error rates, and
**Top tool servers** ranks MCP servers by calls. **Recent traces requiring attention** and
**Top blocking policies** take you straight to problems.

![The Monitoring overview with estimated cost, calls, failure rate, and top models](../assets/screens/monitoring-overview.png "Overview: estimated model cost, model and tool calls, failure rate, blocked traces, and the top models and tool servers.")

### Models: who uses which model, and how many tokens?

Select **Models**. Each row is a responding model with its **Aliases**, **Calls**, **Input tokens**,
**Output tokens**, **Cached input tokens**, **Token share**, error counts, **Caller identities**, and
**Estimated cost**. **Model usage by caller identity** breaks usage and estimated cost down by API key or Entra
caller. That's your first view of cost by API key and model.

> [!NOTE]
> If you see "Model token and estimated cost data are incomplete until you add a Prometheus access token", follow
> the prompt: run `az account get-access-token --resource https://prometheus.monitor.azure.com --query accessToken -o tsv`
> and paste the value into **Prometheus access token**.

### Tools: which MCP tools are called?

Select **Tools**. You see **Total tool calls**, **Active tool servers**, **Usage by tool server**,
**Top tools within tool servers**, and **Tool usage by caller identity**. It stays empty until agents call tools
through the gateway, as in [Federate MCP tools behind one endpoint](../04-federate-mcp-tools/README.md).

### Policies: what did governance block?

Select **Policies**. The summary shows **Requests blocked**, **Caller identities blocked**, and
**Assets with blocked calls**. The table lists each **Policy type** with **Allowed requests**,
**Blocked requests**, and **Last executed**. After [Throttle tokens per caller](../06-token-limits/README.md), the
token limit's `429` responses show up here.

### Traces: find the failed request

Select **Traces**. Each row shows **Time**, **Assets**, **Outcome**, and **Applied policies**. Find the request
for `does-not-exist` from the script, or use **Search trace ID, asset, policy, or reason**.

<!-- /steps -->

> **Checkpoint**
> **Overview** shows the model calls you sent and a non-zero **Estimated model cost**, **Models** shows your API key
> as a caller identity, and **Traces** lists the failed request.

## Follow a request through the trace waterfall

A gateway-aware trace shows where time went and which policies ran, so you can tell a policy rejection from a
backend failure at a glance.

<!-- steps -->

### Open a successful trace

On **Traces**, select a successful model call. The header shows the **Trace ID**, the number of **Spans**, and the
**Duration**.

### Read the waterfall

**Trace waterfall** draws parent-first spans on one timeline. The root span is the model request, for example
`Model · <model-name>` on `POST /default/models/*`. Under it:

| Child span | What it measures |
|---|---|
| **inbound** | Work before the backend call. Each policy that ran is a child span, such as `policy costLimit` with its configuration. |
| **backend** | The call to the provider, for example `HTTP POST` on `/openai/v1/chat/completions`. |
| **outbound** | Work on the response before it returns to the client. |
| **response transfer** | Sending the response back to the client. |

![A trace waterfall with inbound, backend, outbound, and response transfer spans and a cost limit policy span](../assets/screens/monitoring-trace.png "The waterfall splits gateway time from backend time, and each policy that ran appears as its own span.")

### Read the correlated logs

Under **Correlated logs**, expand the request log and switch between **Code** and **Tree**. Look for:

- `gen_ai.operation.name` (for example `chat`), `gen_ai.request.model` (the alias you sent), and
  `gen_ai.response.model` (the versioned model that answered).
- `azure.ai_gateway.client.usage.prompt_tokens`, `...completion_tokens`, and `...total_tokens`: the usage the
  backend reported for this one call.

<!-- /steps -->

> **Checkpoint**
> You can point to the policy spans under **inbound**, compare **backend** time with total time, and read the
> token usage of one request in its correlated log.

## Query telemetry with KQL

The dashboard reads the `OTelSpans` and `OTelLogs` tables in the Log Analytics workspace behind Application Insights.
You can query them directly to build your own reports and alerts.

<!-- steps -->

### Open Logs

In the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com), open the Log Analytics workspace linked to your Application Insights
resource (`<gateway>-logs` if you used the Bicep template) and select **Logs**. Switch the editor to **KQL mode**.

### Run the starter queries

Copy a query from [infra/queries.kql](infra/queries.kql) and run it. Start with query 2 (calls by alias, resolved
model, and API key) and query 3 (token usage per model and API key).

<!-- include: infra/queries.kql kusto -->

On GitHub, open [infra/queries.kql](infra/queries.kql).

These queries are starting points. Attribute names follow the OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions plus gateway
attributes. Run `OTelSpans | take 10` to see what your data carries, and adapt names before you build alerts on
them.

<!-- /steps -->

> **Checkpoint**
> Query 2 returns one row per alias and API key with your call count, and query 3 returns input and output token
> totals that match the order of magnitude on the **Models** tab.

## Verify

<!-- steps -->

### Match the dashboard to your traffic

Run the traffic script once more with five requests, wait a few minutes, and refresh **Monitoring** › **Overview**
with **1H** selected. **Model calls** grows by at least five.

### Confirm all signals are flowing

Open **Settings**. All three signals point at your Application Insights resource, and the dashboard doesn't show
"Enable all telemetry signals".

To check the exporter from the CLI, list the gateway's telemetry exporters:

```bash title="Bash"
az rest --url "$WS/telemetryExporters?$API" --query "value[].{name:name, kind:properties.kind}" -o table
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
az rest --url "$WS/telemetryExporters?$API" --query "value[].{name:name, kind:properties.kind}" -o table
```

The exporter that the portal creates has kind `openTelemetry`. Kind `applicationInsights` is the legacy exporter
from [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting).

<!-- /steps -->

## Go further

- **Query the token metrics.** Token and cost metrics land in the Azure Monitor workspace linked to Application
  Insights as `azure.ai_gateway.client.token.usage` and `azure.ai_gateway.client.token.cost`, with labels such as
  `gen_ai.request.model` and `gen_ai.token.type`. Docs show PromQL in its underscore form, for example
  `sum by (gen_ai_request_model) (gen_ai_client_token_usage)`. Check which names your backend received before you
  build on them. [Attribute tokens and cost with OpenTelemetry](../14-otel-chargeback/README.md) queries them.
- **Alert on what you can act on.** Start with token usage spikes, backend authentication failures, and telemetry
  export failures. Route each alert to an owner who can investigate the gateway, backend, policy, or destination.
- **Send telemetry somewhere else.** Use **Custom OpenTelemetry destination** to export to any OTLP endpoint. Store
  any credential headers as secrets.
- **Capture payloads carefully.** **Settings** › **Logging** has **Log request and response payloads**. It's off by
  default because prompts and responses can be sensitive and add volume.

## Clean up

Application Insights and Log Analytics bill for ingestion and retention. If you continue with
[Attribute tokens and cost with OpenTelemetry](../14-otel-chargeback/README.md), keep everything.

<!-- track: portal | Portal -->

### Disable monitoring

On the **Monitoring** page, select **Settings** › **General** › **Disable monitoring**. This stops the export but
doesn't delete the destination.

### Delete the destination

In the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com), delete the `<gateway>-insights` Application Insights resource and its
Log Analytics workspace if nothing else uses them. Enabling OTLP can also create an Azure Monitor workspace and a
Data Collection Rule for the metrics. Check the resource group for them and delete them if they're unused.

<!-- track: iac | Bicep -->

### Disable monitoring

On the **Monitoring** page, select **Settings** › **General** › **Disable monitoring**.

### Delete the destination

```bash
az resource delete -g "$RG" -n "$GATEWAY-insights" --resource-type Microsoft.Insights/components
az resource delete -g "$RG" -n "$GATEWAY-logs" --resource-type Microsoft.OperationalInsights/workspaces
```

If OTLP setup created an Azure Monitor workspace and a Data Collection Rule, delete them too if they're unused.

<!-- /tracks -->

Keep the gateway, model, and key. The next labs reuse them.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| "Enable all telemetry signals" on the dashboard | Metrics, logs, or traces is turned off | Select **Open Monitoring settings** and set all three endpoints, or disable monitoring and configure it again with Application Insights. |
| "This legacy exporter no longer activates OTLP signals" in **Settings** | The exporter has kind `applicationInsights`, for example from the sample's Bicep or a setup before 2026-08-28 | Select **Settings** › **General** › **Disable monitoring**, then **Configure telemetry** again with the same Application Insights resource. |
| **Assign Monitoring Metrics Publisher role** fails | You can't create role assignments on the destination | Ask an **Owner** to grant the role on the Data Collection Rule, or to run the setup. |
| **Discover OTLP endpoints** fails with "Could not resolve the Data Collection Rule" | OTLP support was just enabled and Azure is still provisioning it | Wait a few minutes, then select **Retry**. |
| "Model token and estimated cost data are incomplete until you add a Prometheus access token" | The portal can't read the metrics workspace with your session | Paste a token from `az account get-access-token --resource https://prometheus.monitor.azure.com --query accessToken -o tsv` into **Prometheus access token**. |
| Dashboard and queries are empty | No traffic in the selected range, or ingestion is still catching up | Widen the time range, wait a few minutes, and run the traffic script again. |

# Attribute tokens and cost with OpenTelemetry

Three teams and a partner tenant share your gateway. Some call it with API keys, others with Microsoft Entra ID.
Finance wants a monthly report of who used which model and what it cost. In this lab you export the right token
claims with the gateway's telemetry, send traffic as both kinds of caller, and build that report from the data
Application Insights already collects.

![AI Gateway exports metrics, logs, and traces with caller attributes](../assets/diagrams/observability.svg "Token claims ride along with the telemetry the gateway already exports, so every log, root trace, and token metric can name its caller.")

## Before you begin

- Complete [Monitor usage, cost, and traces](../13-monitoring/README.md) with **Configure telemetry**, so the
  gateway exports all three signals to Application Insights with an OpenTelemetry exporter.
- Complete [Go keyless with Microsoft Entra ID and RBAC](../11-entra-rbac/README.md), or make sure your signed-in
  user has **AI Gateway Models User** (or **AI Gateway User**) on the gateway or on the model alias.
- Permission to change the gateway, for example **Contributor** on its resource group, and **Log Analytics Reader**
  on the workspace behind Application Insights.
- The [Azure CLI](https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/install-azure-cli) 2.75 or later, signed in with `az login`,
  Python 3.10 or later, and `curl` and `jq` (Bash) or PowerShell 7. The REST track calls the Azure Resource Manager
  REST API with `az rest`, because the `az aigateway` extension doesn't manage the new `aigateways` resource type yet.

Set these variables once. If you named the Application Insights resource differently in lab 13, change
`$GATEWAY-insights`.

```bash title="Bash"
export RG="<resource-group>"
export GATEWAY="<gateway>"
export AI_GATEWAY_MODEL="<model-name>"     # a callable alias
export API="api-version=2025-09-01-preview"

export GATEWAY_ID="$(az resource show -g "$RG" -n "$GATEWAY" --resource-type Microsoft.ApiManagement/aigateways --query id -o tsv)"
export GW="https://management.azure.com$GATEWAY_ID"
export WS="$GW/workspaces/default"
export AI_GATEWAY_URL="https://$(az resource show --ids "$GATEWAY_ID" --query properties.frontend.defaultHostname -o tsv)"
read -rsp "AI Gateway API key: " AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY && export AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY && echo

APPI_ID="$(az resource show -g "$RG" -n "$GATEWAY-insights" --resource-type Microsoft.Insights/components --query id -o tsv)"
LAW_ID="$(az resource show --ids "$APPI_ID" --api-version 2020-02-02 --query properties.WorkspaceResourceId -o tsv)"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$RG      = "<resource-group>"
$GATEWAY = "<gateway>"
$env:AI_GATEWAY_MODEL = "<model-name>"     # a callable alias
$API     = "api-version=2025-09-01-preview"

$GATEWAY_ID = az resource show -g $RG -n $GATEWAY --resource-type Microsoft.ApiManagement/aigateways --query id -o tsv
$GW         = "https://management.azure.com$GATEWAY_ID"
$WS         = "$GW/workspaces/default"
$env:AI_GATEWAY_URL = "https://$(az resource show --ids $GATEWAY_ID --query properties.frontend.defaultHostname -o tsv)"
$env:AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY = Read-Host "AI Gateway API key" -MaskInput

$APPI_ID = az resource show -g $RG -n "$GATEWAY-insights" --resource-type Microsoft.Insights/components --query id -o tsv
$LAW_ID  = az resource show --ids $APPI_ID --api-version 2020-02-02 --query properties.WorkspaceResourceId -o tsv
```

## How it works

Every request already carries its caller. An API key call is attributed by the key's ID
(`azure.ai_gateway.api_key_id`). A Microsoft Entra call carries a validated JWT, and **token claim attributes**
copy the claims you pick into telemetry as `azure.ai_gateway.identity.claims.<claim>`. For each claim you choose the
signals independently: **logs**, **root traces**, and **observed token and cost metrics**.

Logs hold the per-request token usage the backend reported, so they're the best source for a detailed report.
Metrics are cheaper to query over long ranges, but every exported claim value becomes a label, so keep metrics to
claims with a bounded number of values.

Estimated cost is **observed tokens × public pricing**. Treat it as an allocation key and reconcile the total with
provider billing or Azure Cost Management.

| Claim | Identifies | Recommended preset | Use it for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tid` | The caller's tenant | Logs, Traces, Metrics | Tenant or customer totals. With `oid`, the dashboard's Entra caller. |
| `oid` | The user, service principal, or managed identity | Logs, Traces, Metrics | Per-caller totals |
| `appid` (v1 tokens), `azp` (v2 tokens) | The client application | Logs, Traces | Per-app chargeback. This lab adds Metrics. |
| A custom claim, such as `cost_center` | Whatever your tokens carry | You choose | Team chargeback, if the claim is in the token |

## Choose the claims to export

You keep the recommended preset and add **Metrics** for `appid` and `azp`, so token and cost metrics can also be
split by client app.

<!-- track: portal | Portal -->

### Open the token claim attributes

In the [AI Gateway portal](https://ai.gateway.azure.com), select your gateway, then **Monitoring** › **Settings**.
On the **Logging** tab, find **Token claim attributes**: "Add selected JWT claims to exported logs, root traces, and
observed token and cost metrics." Each row is a claim with **Logs**, **Traces**, and **Metrics** checkboxes.

![Monitoring settings with token claim attributes for tid, oid, appid, and azp](../assets/screens/monitoring-token-claim-attributes.png "The recommended preset: tid and oid go to logs, traces, and metrics; appid and azp go to logs and traces.")

> [!NOTE]
> No **Token claim attributes** section? It's only shown for OpenTelemetry exporters. Reconfigure monitoring as
> in [Monitor usage, cost, and traces](../13-monitoring/README.md). If the table is empty ("No token claims are
> included in exported telemetry"), add `tid`, `oid`, `appid`, and `azp` with **Add claim**.

### Add metrics for the client app

Select **Metrics** for `appid` and for `azp`. Leave `tid` and `oid` on all three signals: the dashboard needs
both on metrics to attribute Entra callers. Changes save automatically while "Saving changes…" is shown. Every
claim needs at least one signal.

> [!TIP]
> **Add claim** adds a row (the placeholder suggests `cost_center`) that starts with **Logs** and **Traces**.
> Only add claims that your callers' tokens carry. The next section shows how to check.

<!-- track: rest | REST API -->

### Read the current configuration

The claim attributes live on the gateway's telemetry exporter. List the exporters and their claims:

```bash title="Bash"
az rest --method get --url "$WS/telemetryExporters?$API" \
  --query "value[].{name:name, kind:properties.kind, claims:properties.telemetry.attributes}"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
az rest --method get --url "$WS/telemetryExporters?$API" `
  --query "value[].{name:name, kind:properties.kind, claims:properties.telemetry.attributes}"
```

Expected output: one exporter of kind `openTelemetry`, usually named `appinsights`, whose claims list `tid`, `oid`,
`appid`, and `azp`, each with its `signals`. A kind of `applicationInsights` is the legacy exporter. Reconfigure
monitoring as in [Monitor usage, cost, and traces](../13-monitoring/README.md) first.

### Change it in the portal

The write shape for claim attributes isn't documented for automation yet, so make the change in the portal: open
**Monitoring** › **Settings** › **Logging** › **Token claim attributes** and select **Metrics** for `appid` and
`azp`. Then run the `GET` again. Both claims now list `metrics` in their `signals`.

<!-- /tracks -->

> **Checkpoint**
> `tid` and `oid` export to logs, traces, and metrics, and `appid` and `azp` now export to all three as well.

## Send attributed traffic

<!-- steps -->

### Check what your token carries

A claim only appears in telemetry if the validated token has it. Decode your own token locally and look:

```bash title="Bash"
az account get-access-token --resource https://azure-api.net/aigateway --query accessToken -o tsv \
  | python3 infra/show_claims.py cost_center
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
az account get-access-token --resource https://azure-api.net/aigateway --query accessToken -o tsv |
  python infra/show_claims.py cost_center
```

On GitHub, open [infra/show_claims.py](infra/show_claims.py). The script prints `aud`, `ver`, `tid`, `oid`, `appid`,
`azp`, and `idtyp`, plus any claim names you pass. Nothing leaves your machine.

Expected output: `aud` is `https://azure-api.net/aigateway`, `tid` and `oid` are GUIDs, and either `appid` (v1
token) or `azp` (v2 token) holds the Azure CLI's client ID. `cost_center` is `(not in token)`.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Tokens for AI Gateway are issued for its audience, `https://azure-api.net/aigateway`. Before you add a custom
> claim such as `cost_center` to **Token claim attributes**, decode a real token from that caller and confirm the
> claim is there. If it isn't, map client apps (`appid` or `azp`) to cost centers in your report instead.

### Call the gateway as two callers

Run the script for your shell. It sends five requests with your API key and five with your Entra token, each with an
`x-correlation-id` header.

```bash title="Bash"
./infra/send-attributed-traffic.sh "$AI_GATEWAY_MODEL" 5
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
./infra/send-attributed-traffic.ps1 -Model $env:AI_GATEWAY_MODEL -Requests 5
```

On GitHub, open [send-attributed-traffic.sh](infra/send-attributed-traffic.sh) or
[send-attributed-traffic.ps1](infra/send-attributed-traffic.ps1).

Expected output: ten rows, all `200`, alternating between `api-key` and `entra`. A `401` or `403` on the `entra`
rows means your role assignment is missing or hasn't propagated yet.

### Find your callers in Monitoring

Wait a few minutes, then open **Monitoring** › **Models** with **1H** selected. In
**Model usage by caller identity**, your API key and your Entra identity appear as separate rows with their own
tokens and estimated cost. Entra callers are resolved from `tid` and `oid`. Callers with neither an API key nor
those claims show as **Unattributed**.

Then select **Traces**, open one of the Entra requests, and expand its log under **Correlated logs**. Look for
`azure.ai_gateway.identity.claims.tid`, `...oid`, and `...appid` or `...azp`. An API key request shows
`azure.ai_gateway.api_key_id` instead.

<!-- /steps -->

> **Checkpoint**
> Both callers appear on the **Models** tab, and an Entra request's correlated log shows its claims.

## Build a chargeback report

The report groups the token usage in request logs by owner and prices it with a price list you control. The query
is in [infra/chargeback.kql](infra/chargeback.kql):

<!-- include: infra/chargeback.kql kusto -->

On GitHub, open [infra/chargeback.kql](infra/chargeback.kql).

<!-- steps -->

### Prepare a price list

Copy [infra/prices.example.json](infra/prices.example.json) to `prices.json`. Replace `<model-name>` with each value
in the report's `Model` column, which is the model that answered (for example a versioned name), and copy current
prices per million tokens from your provider's pricing page or agreement. A versioned name such as
`my-model-2026-01-01` matches the key `my-model`.

> [!CAUTION]
> The example prices are placeholders. Don't publish a report until you've replaced them with real prices.

<!-- /steps -->

<!-- track: portal | Portal -->

### Run the query

In the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com), open the Log Analytics workspace behind your Application Insights
resource and select **Logs**. Switch to **KQL mode**, paste the contents of `infra/chargeback.kql`, and select
**Run**. You get one row per tenant, object ID, client app, API key, alias, and model.

### Export it

Select **Export** and choose CSV with all columns. Save the file as `usage.csv` in the lab folder.

### Price it

```bash title="Bash"
python3 infra/chargeback_report.py usage.csv prices.json --by Tenant,ClientApp,ApiKeyId --out chargeback.csv
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
python infra/chargeback_report.py usage.csv prices.json --by Tenant,ClientApp,ApiKeyId --out chargeback.csv
```

<!-- track: rest | REST API -->

### Run the query

Send the query to the Log Analytics query API through Azure Resource Manager and save the response:

```bash title="Bash"
jq -n --rawfile q infra/chargeback.kql '{query: $q}' > query.json
az rest --method post \
  --url "https://management.azure.com${LAW_ID}/query?api-version=2017-10-01" \
  --body @query.json > usage.json
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
@{ query = Get-Content infra/chargeback.kql -Raw } | ConvertTo-Json | Set-Content query.json
az rest --method post `
  --url "https://management.azure.com$LAW_ID/query?api-version=2017-10-01" `
  --body "@query.json" | Set-Content usage.json
```

The response holds a `tables` array with `columns` and `rows`, which the report script reads directly.

### Price it

```bash title="Bash"
python3 infra/chargeback_report.py usage.json prices.json --by Tenant,ClientApp,ApiKeyId --out chargeback.csv
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
python infra/chargeback_report.py usage.json prices.json --by Tenant,ClientApp,ApiKeyId --out chargeback.csv
```

<!-- /tracks -->

On GitHub, open [infra/chargeback_report.py](infra/chargeback_report.py). It sums requests and tokens per group,
prices uncached input, cached input, and output tokens separately, and lists any model without a price. Group by
any column from the query, for example `--by CostCenter` or `--by ApiKeyId,Model`.

Expected output: a table with one row for your API key (`(none)` in `Tenant` and `ClientApp`) and one for your
Entra identity (your tenant ID and the Azure CLI's client ID), followed by a total.

> [!TIP]
> The report shows IDs. Resolve a client app's name with
> `az ad sp show --id <client-app-id> --query displayName -o tsv`, and an API key's name under **Access** › **Keys**.

> **Checkpoint**
> `chargeback.csv` has a priced row for each caller, and no model is listed under "No price for".

## Query token and cost metrics with PromQL

Token and cost metrics land in the Azure Monitor workspace (managed Prometheus) linked to Application Insights, as
`azure.ai_gateway.client.token.usage` and `azure.ai_gateway.client.token.cost`. They're the same metrics the
dashboard reads, and they carry the claims you enabled for **Metrics** as labels.

<!-- steps -->

### Find the Prometheus endpoint

```bash title="Bash"
AMW_ID="$(az resource show --ids "$APPI_ID" --api-version 2020-02-02 --query properties.AzureMonitorWorkspaceResourceId -o tsv)"
PROM_URL="$(az resource show --ids "$AMW_ID" --api-version 2023-04-03 --query properties.metrics.prometheusQueryEndpoint -o tsv)"
PROM_TOKEN="$(az account get-access-token --resource https://prometheus.monitor.azure.com --query accessToken -o tsv)"
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$AMW_ID     = az resource show --ids $APPI_ID --api-version 2020-02-02 --query properties.AzureMonitorWorkspaceResourceId -o tsv
$PROM_URL   = az resource show --ids $AMW_ID --api-version 2023-04-03 --query properties.metrics.prometheusQueryEndpoint -o tsv
$PROM_TOKEN = az account get-access-token --resource https://prometheus.monitor.azure.com --query accessToken -o tsv
```

### Query token usage for the last day

The metric names contain dots, so the selector uses quoted names. The `microsoft.appresourceid` label limits the
query to your Application Insights resource.

```bash title="Bash"
SELECTOR="{__name__=\"azure.ai_gateway.client.token.usage\",\"microsoft.appresourceid\"=\"$(echo "$APPI_ID" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')\"}"
curl -sS -G "${PROM_URL%/}/api/v1/query" -H "Authorization: Bearer $PROM_TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode "query=increase(${SELECTOR}[1d])" \
  | jq -r '.data.result[] | [.metric["gen_ai.response.model"], .metric["gen_ai.token.type"],
      (.metric["azure.ai_gateway.api_key_id"] // "-"), (.metric["azure.ai_gateway.identity.claims.tid"] // "-"),
      (.metric["azure.ai_gateway.identity.claims.appid"] // .metric["azure.ai_gateway.identity.claims.azp"] // "-"),
      (.value[1] | tonumber | round)] | @tsv'
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
$selector = '{__name__="azure.ai_gateway.client.token.usage","microsoft.appresourceid"="' + $APPI_ID.ToLower() + '"}'
$result = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "$($PROM_URL.TrimEnd('/'))/api/v1/query" `
  -Headers @{ Authorization = "Bearer $PROM_TOKEN" } -Body @{ query = 'increase(' + $selector + '[1d])' }
$result.data.result | ForEach-Object { [pscustomobject]@{
  Model     = $_.metric.'gen_ai.response.model'
  TokenType = $_.metric.'gen_ai.token.type'
  ApiKeyId  = $_.metric.'azure.ai_gateway.api_key_id'
  Tenant    = $_.metric.'azure.ai_gateway.identity.claims.tid'
  ClientApp = $_.metric.'azure.ai_gateway.identity.claims.appid' ?? $_.metric.'azure.ai_gateway.identity.claims.azp'
  Tokens    = [math]::Round([double]$_.value[1]) } } | Format-Table
```

Expected output: rows per model, token type, and caller. Your Entra rows carry your tenant ID and the client app.

> [!WARNING]
> Don't add up every token type. A model reports totals and details (for example `total_tokens` and
> `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`) next to input and output, so a plain sum double counts. Use the total
> type if there is one, otherwise input plus output. Cached tokens are usually a subset of input tokens.

### Query estimated cost

Replace `azure.ai_gateway.client.token.usage` with `azure.ai_gateway.client.token.cost` and run the query again. Each
series carries `azure.ai_gateway.currency`. Series with `azure.ai_gateway.price_missing="true"` had no public price,
so their cost isn't counted.

<!-- /steps -->

> [!NOTE]
> Counters are cumulative, and `increase()` extrapolates and can miss the first sample of a brand new series, so
> treat short-range metric results as approximate. The docs show PromQL in its underscore form,
> `sum by (gen_ai_request_model) (gen_ai_client_token_usage)`, which is how some OTLP backends store these names.
> If a query returns nothing, list the names your backend stored with `count by (__name__) ({__name__=~".*token.*"})`.

## Verify

<!-- steps -->

### Compare the report with the dashboard

Open **Monitoring** › **Models** with **24H** selected. The input and output tokens of your two callers in
**Model usage by caller identity** are in the same range as their rows in `chargeback.csv`.

### Confirm the client app label

Run the PromQL query again. Your Entra rows show a client app ID, which comes from the **Metrics** signal you
enabled for `appid` and `azp`.

<!-- /steps -->

## Go further

- **Enforce what you measure.** A cost limit can give a different budget to a specific Entra identity or to a
  **Custom token claim combination**, such as an `appid` value. See
  [Enforce cost budgets with per-caller overrides](../07-cost-budgets/README.md).
- **Send telemetry to another backend.** In the setup wizard, **Custom OpenTelemetry destination** takes a
  **Metrics endpoint**, **Logs endpoint**, and **Traces endpoint**, such as a collector, Grafana, Datadog, or any
  OTLP service. Authenticate with **Custom headers** (values are masked and never shown again after saving) or a
  **Managed identity** with a token audience. Claims are exported the same way. The built-in dashboard only reads
  Application Insights, so with a custom destination you build these views in that platform.
- **Fan out with a collector.** To keep claims in one place and send them to several backends, point the gateway at
  your own OpenTelemetry Collector and route from there.
- **Keep metric cardinality in check.** Every distinct claim value is a new series. Put high-cardinality claims such
  as `oid` on logs and traces for detail, and keep metrics to `tid`, client apps, and bounded custom claims.
- **Schedule the report.** Run the REST track monthly from a pipeline with a managed identity that has
  **Log Analytics Reader**, and store `chargeback.csv` with your finance data.

## Clean up

The exported files contain tenant and object IDs. Treat them as personal data.

<!-- track: portal | Portal -->

### Restore the preset

In **Monitoring** › **Settings** › **Logging** › **Token claim attributes**, clear **Metrics** for `appid` and
`azp`. Remove any custom claim you added.

### Delete the exported files

Delete `usage.csv`, `prices.json`, and `chargeback.csv` from the lab folder.

<!-- track: rest | REST API -->

### Restore the preset

In **Monitoring** › **Settings** › **Logging** › **Token claim attributes**, clear **Metrics** for `appid` and
`azp`, then run the `GET` from the start of the lab to confirm both claims list only `logs` and `traces`.

### Delete the exported files

```bash title="Bash"
rm -f query.json usage.json prices.json chargeback.csv
```

```powershell title="PowerShell"
Remove-Item query.json, usage.json, prices.json, chargeback.csv -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
```

<!-- /tracks -->

Keep monitoring on if you continue: the agent labs use it to show where agent calls went. Otherwise, follow the
clean-up steps in [Monitor usage, cost, and traces](../13-monitoring/README.md).

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| No **Token claim attributes** section in **Settings** | The exporter is the legacy `applicationInsights` kind | Disable monitoring and configure it again, as in [Monitor usage, cost, and traces](../13-monitoring/README.md). |
| The `entra` rows return `401` or `403` | Wrong token audience, or no **AI Gateway Models User** role yet | Get the token for `https://azure-api.net/aigateway`, check the role assignment, wait a few minutes, and get a new token. |
| Entra callers show as **Unattributed** on **Models** | `tid` or `oid` isn't exported to **Metrics** | Select **Metrics** for both and send new traffic. Earlier requests stay unattributed. |
| The chargeback query returns no rows | Telemetry hasn't arrived, the **Logs** signal is off, or your API reports usage under other names | Wait a few minutes, then run `OTelLogs \| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h) \| take 5` and compare the `Attributes` with the query. |
| `Tenant` or `ClientApp` is empty for Entra rows | The claim wasn't exported to **Logs** when the request ran | Enable **Logs** for the claim and send new traffic. |
| The Prometheus query returns `401` or `403` | Your account can't read the Azure Monitor workspace | Ask for a data read role on the Azure Monitor workspace, such as **Monitoring Data Reader**, then get a new token. |
